title: PR #44653: Validate buffer slices during deserialization
body:
PR #44653: Validate buffer slices during deserialization

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/44653

## Summary

- validate `BufferAllocation::Slice::FromProto` rejects negative offsets and sizes
- reject serialized slices whose `[offset, offset + size)` range exceeds the referenced allocation
- add regression coverage for malformed `BufferAllocationSliceProto` values

## Why

`BufferAllocation::Slice::FromProto` reconstructs runtime buffer slices from serialized executable data. It previously validated only `buffer_allocation_index`, while the compile-time assignment path guarantees that `offset >= 0`, `size >= 0`, and `offset + size <= allocation.size()`. This change enforces that same invariant before constructing the slice.

## Testing

- `git diff --check`
- `clang++ -std=c++17 -fsanitize=address -g -DNDEBUG -DAPPLY_FIX poc_primitive_asan.cc -o /tmp/openxla_poc_fixed && /tmp/openxla_poc_fixed` from the local reproduction bundle; the fixed logic rejects the malformed slice
- attempted `bazel test //xla/service:buffer_assignment_test`; local sparse-checkout setup initially missed top-level `third_party` and `tools`, and after adding them the invocation stayed in Bazel repository mapping until interrupted. Retrying with `--noexperimental_repo_remote_exec` fails during repository initialization because `rules_ml_toolchain` requires that experimental flag.

title: PR #45682: pjrt: propagate Prepare failure on non-two-phase multi-device Execute
body:
PR #45682: pjrt: propagate Prepare failure on non-two-phase multi-device Execute

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45682

## The bug

`CommonPjRtLoadedExecutable::Execute`'s multi-device path calls `ExecutePrepareWithOomRetries` per device, then — only when `supports_two_phase_launch()` is true — checks the returned status inside the two-phase barrier block. `CpuClient` overrides `supports_two_phase_launch()` to `false`, so on a multi-device CpuClient a Prepare failure is never checked and execution falls through to `ExecuteLaunch(*launch_args, ...)` with `launch_args.executable` still null → null-deref crash instead of a clean error.

## The fix

Add an `else if (!launch_status.ok())` branch after the two-phase block: record the failure in `results[i]`, decrement `launching` under `mu`, return. Same shape as the two-phase failure path minus the barrier it doesn't participate in.

## Scope

`CpuClient` is the only in-tree client with `supports_two_phase_launch()==false`. Two-phase clients (GPU/TPU stream-executor) are unchanged — the diff is purely additive.

## Test

`MultiDevicePrepareFailurePropagatesError` in `[cpu_client_test.cc](http://cpu_client_test.cc/)`: 2-device CpuClient, 2-replica identity program, wrong-size buffer on device 1 so `CheckBufferCompatibilities` rejects it during Prepare. Asserts `Execute()` returns an error (not a crash) and that the error comes from the per-device Prepare path.

Since `ValidateCreateOptions` rejects unrecognized keys, passing `"max_inflight_computations"` via the plugin path (e.g. JAX's `jax_pjrt_client_create_options`) fails client creation with `Unexpected option name passed to PJRT_Client_Create`, so the field can't be set from Python.

This PR adds the key to `kExpectedOptionNameAndTypes` and forwards it to `GpuClientOptions`. The value is validated to be in `(0, INT32_MAX]`: the field is `int`, and a zero value would construct a compute semaphore that blocks forever on the first `Execute()`. When the option is omitted, the `GpuClientOptions` default (32) is preserved; disabling the semaphore entirely (`std::nullopt`) remains C++-only, since expressing "no limit" through an int64 option would need a sentinel value.

This is GPU-specific because `"max_inflight_computations"` is already among the TPU plugin's published create-option names (`pjrt::tpu_configs::kMaxInflightComputations`, `xla/pjrt/c/pjrt_c_api_tpu_constants.h`); this change brings the GPU plugin to parity.

title: PR #45596: [XLA:GPU] Support VA remapping of output buffer allocations
body:
PR #45596: [XLA:GPU] Support VA remapping of output buffer allocations

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45596

## 📝 Summary of Changes

This PR extends command-buffer virtual-address remapping to allocations that
escape to the caller (`maybe_live_out`) while preserving the const ownership
model introduced by #45595.

- Keeps selected live-out allocations at normal allocator-owned addresses in
  the owning `BufferAllocations` table.
- Extends `GetRemappedBufferAllocations` to map finalized selected input/output
  addresses into their stable reservation slices immediately before execution.
- Rewrites only the non-owning execution copy, so result handling and teardown
  continue to see external, deallocatable addresses.
- Handles donated and copy-protected aliases by mapping after output setup has
  finalized the owning address table.
- Extends the host-only fake-VMM tests to cover stable execution aliases,
  logical external sizes, output deallocation, and deferred alias cleanup.

This PR is stacked on #45595, **[XLA:GPU] Support VA remapping of parameter
buffer allocations**. It is part 2 of 3 splitting the former #45568
implementation; #45597 adds the `SKIP_PROFILED` mode.

## 🎯 Justification

Live-out buffers can outlive an execution scope, so the caller must retain a
normal allocator-owned address that remains valid and can be passed to
`Deallocate()`. At the same time, recorded command buffers need a stable
reservation address.

Building a separate execution allocation table provides both properties
without mutating the owning table or removing its const qualifier. Deferring
the mapping until execution also ensures donation and copy protection have
already selected the final external address.

## 🚀 Kind of Contribution

✨ New Feature

## 📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)

Not applicable as a standalone change. This PR adds output-buffer remapping
support but does not independently enable a new command-buffer update mode.
Performance evaluation belongs to the final `SKIP_PROFILED` policy in #45597.

## 🧪 Unit Tests:

- Extends the host-only fake-VMM allocator test with a non-granularity-aligned
  remapped live-out allocation.
- Verifies the owning table contains the logical-size external address before
  and after execution.
- Verifies execution receives the same stable reservation address across runs
  and maps the correct raw physical allocation.
- Verifies the external address is deallocatable and all aliases are released.

## 🧪 Execution Tests:

No standalone execution test is added for this enabling layer. End-to-end
live-out selection, execution, and output deallocation are covered by the
stacked `SKIP_PROFILED` change in #45597.

title: Fix NaN gradient of tf.math.igamma at a=1, x=0
body:
Fixes #123578

 _IgammaGrad computed partial_x = exp(-x + (a-1)*log(x) - lgamma(a)).
  
At a==1, x==0 the term (a-1)*log(x) is 0 * -inf = NaN, so the gradient of tf.math.igamma w.r.t. x is NaN there. The true derivative is d/dx igamma(1, x) = e^-x = 1. Use xlogy(a-1, x) instead, matching _BetaincGrad which already does this. Other regimes unchanged (a>1 -> 0, a<1 -> +inf, nonzero x identical). Adds IgammaGradTest.

Reproduced on tf-nightly 2.22.0-dev20260718.

title: Fix WatchGlobalProcessInfo infinite retry on service incarnation mismatch
body:
Fix WatchGlobalProcessInfo infinite retry on service incarnation mismatch

When the coordination service restarts (e.g., after task preemption
triggers a full pod reallocation), surviving tasks hold a stale
service incarnation ID. Their WatchTasksAsync RPCs fail with
"wrong service incarnation", and the WatchGlobalProcessInfo loop
retries indefinitely because it never checks the agent error state.

Check agent.IsError() after a failed WatchTasksAsync. If the agent
has entered an unrecoverable ERROR state (set by the WatchTasksAsync
callback on incarnation mismatch), return the error instead of
retrying. Transient errors that do not trigger SetError continue
to be retried.

Validation: tested on a 256-chip (64-task) multi-host JAX workload
where a single task hit a coordination shutdown barrier timeout
(DEADLINE_EXCEEDED, 63/64 tasks reached barrier). Without the fix,
all remaining tasks entered an infinite retry loop logging "wrong
service incarnation" and hung indefinitely, requiring manual kill.
With the fix, the agent.IsError() check detected the unrecoverable
ERROR state and returned immediately, allowing all tasks to exit
cleanly via std::quick_exit(42) with no manual intervention.

title: Fix host memory leak in tf.data.Dataset.from_generator during eager execution
body:
## Bug fix: host RAM leak in `tf.data.Dataset.from_generator` (#123269)

**Reproduction:** Running `from_generator` in a loop leaks ~128 MB of host RSS over 500 iterations even after `del dataset` and `gc.collect()`. GPU VRAM is unaffected.

## Root cause

Every call to `from_generator` traces three closures via `StructuredFunctionWrapper` (`init_func`, `next_func`, `finalize_func`). During tracing those closures call `numpy_function` / `eager_py_func`, which routes through `_internal_py_func` in `script_ops.py`. There, a **strong reference** to each closure is stored:

```python
# script_ops.py – the leak
graph = ops.get_default_graph()
while True:          # walk up to outermost non-FuncGraph
    ...
graph._py_funcs_used_in_graph.append(func)   # ← accumulates forever
```

In eager mode the outermost non-FuncGraph is the **process-lifetime singleton** returned by `ops.get_default_graph()`. It is never destroyed, so `_py_funcs_used_in_graph` grows indefinitely. After 500 iterations, ~1 500 closures accumulate there (each capturing a `generator_state` object), accounting for the ~128 MB RSS growth.

## Fix

When `_internal_py_func` is called while already executing inside a `FuncGraph` (as happens during `StructuredFunctionWrapper` tracing), skip the walk-to-outermost-graph and keep the strong reference on the **FuncGraph itself**:

```python
if not isinstance(graph, func_graph.FuncGraph):
    while True:   # only walk up when NOT already in a FuncGraph
        ...
graph._py_funcs_used_in_graph.append(func)
```

The `FuncGraph`'s lifetime is tied to its `ConcreteFunction` → `StructuredFunctionWrapper` → `Dataset`. When `del dataset` runs and GC collects the chain, the `FuncGraph` is dismantled, `_py_funcs_used_in_graph` on it is released, and all three closures (and their `generator_state` captures) are freed.

In graph mode and in eager mode outside any `FuncGraph` the original behaviour is preserved unchanged.

Fixes #123269

title: Avoid grabbing the `TileAssignment` mutex in the common case.
body:
Avoid grabbing the `TileAssignment` mutex in the common case.

Before this change, many trivial accessor fuctions in `TileAssignment`
would acquire the mutex protecting the materialized array. This is
especially unfortunate for accessors like `num_dimensions()`, which can
be called in loops and which should always be able to obtain the value
cheaply (without acquiring any locks) from either `iota_` or the
materialized array.

This change makes `array_` an atomic pointer to enable it to be accessed
without locking. Accessors that can use either `iota_` or `array_` are
changed to try `iota_` by default unless obtaining the value from
`array_` is cheaper. After this change, the mutex is only acquired when
we materialize the array or access `shared_array_`.

title: [PJRT] Add support for UndonatableCommonPjRtBuffer and CommonPjRtClient::MakeUndonatable.
body:
[PJRT] Add support for UndonatableCommonPjRtBuffer and CommonPjRtClient::MakeUndonatable.

Provide a factory `MakeUndonatable` for turning an existing buffer into an `UndonatableCommonPjRtBuffer`, it consumes the input buffer and returns an equivalent hold-free buffer aliasing the same device memory. It uses CommonPjRtClient's friend access on CommonPjRtBuffer to donate the tracked buffer, snapshotting the underlying raw buffer along with its definition events to construct UndonatableCommonPjRtBuffer.

Static factory `UndonatableCommonPjRtBuffer::Create` is provided as a helper on the buffer class that delegates to `CommonPjRtClient::MakeUndonatable`. Unit tests in `undonatable_common_pjrt_buffer_test.cc` have been updated to use the factory and include null-check verification.

title: PR #45263: Allow dynamic-update-slice into an unbounded-dynamic operand dimension
body:
PR #45263: Allow dynamic-update-slice into an unbounded-dynamic operand dimension

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45263

### Problem
`InferDynamicUpdateSliceShape` rejects a valid `dynamic-update-slice` into an **unbounded-dynamic** operand dimension.

### Root cause
```cpp
const int64_t input_dim_size = operand_shape.dimensions(dim);
...
if (update_dim_size > input_dim_size) {   // input_dim_size == kUnboundedSize (INT64_MIN) for an unbounded dim
  return InvalidArgument("Update dim size %d greater than dynamic slice dimension: %d.", ...);
}
```
For an unbounded-dynamic operand dimension, `operand_shape.dimensions(dim)` is `kUnboundedSize` (`INT64_MIN`). Any concrete static update size (e.g. `5`) then satisfies `5 > INT64_MIN` and the op is rejected with a nonsensical bound (`-9223372036854775808`). The sibling `InferDynamicSliceShape` guards the identical comparison with `!IsUnboundedDynamicSize(input_dim_size)`, and this function already handles unbounded *update* sizes just above — so unbounded operands are in scope, but the operand side is unguarded.

### Fix
Guard with `!IsUnboundedDynamicSize(input_dim_size)`, matching `InferDynamicSliceShape`.

### Verification
Static reasoning: e.g. `operand = f32[?, 10]`, `update = f32[3, 5]` is rejected today (`3 > INT64_MIN`) and accepted with the fix; operand-static-with-too-large-update still errors; both-unbounded and operand-static-with-unbounded-update are unchanged. (No local Bazel build set up — happy to add a shape-inference test.)

title: PR #45816: [XLA:GPU] Don't let rank-0 dimension-size scalars inherit op sharding
body:
PR #45816: [XLA:GPU] Don't let rank-0 dimension-size scalars inherit op sharding

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45816

📝 Summary of Changes
Stop rank-0 dimension-size scalars from inheriting the enclosing op's sharding.

title: Fix heap out-of-bounds write in CTC loss with empty target sequence
body:
### Summary

Fixes #123396 — a heap out-of-bounds write in the native CTC loss CPU
implementation that AddressSanitizer reports as a `bad-free` when calling
`tf.raw_ops.CTCLoss` with a minimal single-class configuration.

### Root cause

`CTCLossOp` hardcodes the blank label as `num_classes - 1`. With
`inputs` shape `[1, 1, 1]`, `num_classes == 1`, so the blank index is `0`.
A label value of `0` therefore equals the blank and is treated as a
"null/finished" label in `PopulateLPrimes`, collapsing the target to an
empty sequence. `GetLPrimeIndices` then produces `l_prime = [blank]`, so
`U = l_prime.size() == 1`.

Two initialization sites in `ctc_loss_calculator.h` assume `U >= 2` and
write outside the `U x T` (here `1 x 1`) alpha/beta matrices:

- `CalculateForwardVariables` unconditionally wrote `log_alpha->coeffRef(1, 0)`
  (row 1 of a 1-row matrix). The surrounding code already anticipated
  `U == 1` via the `l_prime.size() > 1 ? l_prime[1] : blank_index_` ternary,
  but the write itself was not guarded.
- `CalculateBackwardVariables` looped `for (int u = U - 2; u < U; ++u)`,
  starting at `u == -1` and writing `log_beta->coeffRef(-1, T - 1)`.

Both are heap out-of-bounds writes that corrupt the Eigen matrix
allocation metadata, later surfacing as the ASan `bad-free`.

### Fix

Complete the already-intended `U == 1` handling:

- Guard the second-row `log_alpha` initialization behind `if (U > 1)`.
- Clamp the `log_beta` initialization lower bound with `std::max(0, U - 2)`.

The degenerate empty-target case now computes a finite loss
(`-log P(all blanks)`) and gradient instead of corrupting the heap. The
`U > 1` path is unchanged.

### Test

Adds `testSingleClassBlankOnlyLabel` to `ctc_loss_op_test.py`, which
reproduces the exact minimal input from the issue and asserts a finite
loss and gradient of the expected shapes. Runs in both graph and eager
modes. Without the fix this test crashes the process under ASan; with it,
it passes.

### Notes

- No API or behavioral change for valid CTC inputs; only the previously
  crashing degenerate case is affected.

title: [IFRT] Copy serialized Cord to std::string during deserialization to avoid ASan buffer overflow
body:
[IFRT] Copy serialized Cord to std::string during deserialization to avoid ASan buffer overflow

MLIR Lexer (used by the text/assembly parser) assumes the input buffer is null-terminated. When parsing text-based StableHLO or IFRT IR during deserialization, `deserializePortableArtifact` and `ParseMlirModuleString` receive a non-null-terminated `absl::string_view` from `absl::Cord::Flatten()`. If an identifier ends exactly at the buffer boundary, the lexer reads past the end of the buffer, causing an ASan `stack-buffer-overflow`.

To fix this safely across remaining callsites, we copy the serialized data to a `std::string` to guarantee null-termination before passing it to MLIR parsing or string parsing utilities.

title: PR #45595: [XLA:GPU] Support VA remapping of parameter buffer allocations
body:
PR #45595: [XLA:GPU] Support VA remapping of parameter buffer allocations

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45595

## 📝 Summary of Changes

This PR extends command-buffer virtual-address remapping to entry-computation parameter allocations. Parameter buffers remain caller-owned, so each execution aliases their physical memory into stable VA-reservation addresses instead of transferring ownership to the VMM allocator.

- Adds `ExecutionScope::ResolveParameterBuffer`; the base implementation returns the caller buffer, while the VA-remapping implementation installs and returns the stable reservation alias.
- Renames the `PrepareReservation` hook to `Prepare` and makes `ExecuteWithBufferAllocations` accept mutable `BufferAllocations`, allowing addresses to be restored after execution.
- Tracks per-execution parameter aliases with `RecordStepAlias`.
- Releases those aliases after every execution and rewrites remapped entries back to their caller-owned addresses before teardown and result handling. The execution-scope destructor provides cleanup for error paths.
- Adds `AddVaRemappedAllocationForTesting` and a host-only fake VMM allocator to exercise the parameter-remapping path without requiring a GPU.

This PR is stacked on #45567, **[XLA:GPU] Split command buffer VA remapping into its own allocator class**. It is part 1 of 3 splitting the former #45568 implementation into reviewable changes; #45596 adds output-buffer remapping and #45597 adds the `SKIP_PROFILED` mode.

## 🎯 Justification

`SKIP_TEMP` stabilizes only preallocated temporary buffers, but profiled command-buffer update policies also need to stabilize caller-owned parameters whose physical addresses remain constant across executions. Parameter ownership prevents allocating them directly through the command-buffer reservation.

Creating a per-execution alias gives recorded command buffers a stable VA while preserving the caller's original address and ownership. Restoring the original address after execution ensures teardown and result handling never observe a reservation address.

## 🚀 Kind of Contribution

✨ New Feature

## 📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)

Not applicable as a standalone change. This PR adds parameter-remapping support but does not select it in a production update mode. Performance evaluation belongs to the final `SKIP_PROFILED` policy in #45597.

## 🧪 Unit Tests:

- Added host-only `gpu_executable_va_remap_allocator_test.cc` coverage using a fake VMM allocator.
- Verifies that a caller-owned parameter receives the same stable reservation address across executions.
- Verifies persistent allocation-index handling, post-execution restoration to the caller address, and release of each per-execution mapping.
- Covers cleanup behavior without requiring a GPU.

## 🧪 Execution Tests:

No standalone execution test is added because no production update mode selects parameter allocations in this PR. End-to-end selection and execution coverage is provided by the stacked `SKIP_PROFILED` change in #45597.

title: [XLA:GPU] Rewrite seeded and live carry add scans to CUB device scans.
body:
[XLA:GPU] Rewrite seeded and live carry add scans to CUB device scans.

The CUB scan rewriter only matched forward add scans with an all zero
scalar init and a dead final carry. The forms this CL matches did not
reach the reduce window rewriter's tree lowering either (it rejects
reverse scans and live carry users and fails compilation on non
scalar inits), so they lowered to sequential while loops or failed
outright, and the reverse support already plumbed to the kernel was
unreachable. By associativity, a seeded inclusive add scan is the
unseeded scan plus the broadcast seed, and its final carry is the
boundary output element. Rewrite non zero inits as one elementwise
add of the broadcast init to the CUB result, feed live final carry
users a slice of the output at the last scanned position, and match
reverse scans. With this, scans that the SPMD partitioner shards on
their scan dimension lower to per shard CUB scans instead of while
loops.

title: Properly move iota_ (`std::move(other.iota_)`) and null out other.array_ (`std::exchange(other.array_, nullptr)`) inside TileAssignment move constructor and move assignment operator.
body:
Properly move iota_ (`std::move(other.iota_)`) and null out other.array_ (`std::exchange(other.array_, nullptr)`) inside TileAssignment move constructor and move assignment operator.

When `HloSharding` is moved around and assigned over during XLA passes such as `XPrecisionRewriter` (`ReplaceInstruction`), leaving `other.array_` non-null inside the moved-from `TileAssignment` while moving out `shared_array_` causes dangling pointers and aliased deallocations upon subsequent array access or assignment. Furthermore, copying `iota_` (`std::optional<IotaTileAssignment>`) instead of moving it creates duplicate internal allocations.

Using `std::move` and `std::exchange` ensures clean transfer of pointer ownership and prevents `free(): invalid pointer` crashes.

title: [IFRT] Copy serialized Cord to std::string during deserialization to avoid ASan buffer overflow
body:
[IFRT] Copy serialized Cord to std::string during deserialization to avoid ASan buffer overflow

MLIR Lexer (used by the text/assembly parser) assumes the input buffer is null-terminated.
When parsing text-based StableHLO during deserialization (e.g. on invalid input in tests), `deserializePortableArtifact` receives a non-null-terminated `absl::string_view` from `absl::Cord::Flatten()`.
If an identifier ends exactly at the buffer boundary, the lexer reads past the end of the buffer, causing an ASan `stack-buffer-overflow`.

To fix this safely, we copy the serialized data to a `std::string` to guarantee null-termination before passing it to MLIR parsing. Since this only happens during program deserialization (non-hot path), the performance impact is expected to be low, but we will need to do a follow-up if the extra cost turns out to be too high.

title: Modify CommonPjRtClient to use ExecuteArgHold for execution arguments to support undonatable buffers.
body:
Modify CommonPjRtClient to use ExecuteArgHold for execution arguments to support undonatable buffers.

This change introduces `ExecuteArgHold` as a variant type (`std::variant<PjRtRawBufferRef, CommonPjRtBuffer::ScopedHold>`) to support execution with `UndonatableCommonPjRtBuffer`.
`UndonatableCommonPjRtBuffer` enforces lifetime via reference counting alone using `PjRtRawBufferRef` (acquired via `AcquireRawBufferRef()`) as its hold mechanism. `ExecuteArgHold` allows `CommonPjRtClient` to hold execution argument references for both buffer types. Additionally, definition events for undonatable buffers are inspected during argument preparation to propagate errors and dependencies.

title: [TF:Core] Synchronize DirectSession destructor with active Run calls to prevent UAF.
body:
[TF:Core] Synchronize DirectSession destructor with active Run calls to prevent UAF.

Use lock-free atomic reference counting (`std::atomic<int> active_runs_`) via RAII `RunScope` (`fetch_add`/`fetch_sub`) on `Run()`, `RunCallable()`, `MakeCallable()`, `PRunSetup()`, and `PRun()` execution paths to track active executions. In `DirectSession::~DirectSession()`, execute a bounded 50ms polling loop (`absl::SleepFor`) with a default 60s ceiling (configurable via `TF_SESSION_DESTRUCTOR_WAIT_SECONDS`) until `active_runs_` reaches zero before tearing down session state. This mitigates heap Use-After-Free (UAF) crashes caused by concurrent query or session cancellation.

title: PR #45422: [XLA:SE] Consolidate VMM allocator mapped allocation paths
body:
PR #45422: [XLA:SE] Consolidate VMM allocator mapped allocation paths

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45422

Stack:

1. #45419 — reclaim tests, PA accounting, and typed overlap filters
2. #45420 — map resolution
3. #45421 — allocation-record and pending-operation state
4. #45422 — mapped allocation reuse and creation

This is the fourth and final PR in a four-part DeviceAddressVmmAllocator cleanup stack and is stacked on #45421. PR #45323 is intentionally left unchanged.

📝 Summary of Changes

- Represent the two mapped-allocation address layouts with an explicit `MappedAddressMode` request field.
- Replace separate reservation-address and separate-address reuse helpers with one `TryReuseMappedAllocation` implementation.
- Replace the corresponding creation helpers with one `CreateMappedAllocation` implementation.
- Return the tracked allocation record directly from record installation and tighten checks around mapping, retry, and pending-reclaim transitions.

title: PR #45567: [XLA:GPU] Split command buffer VA remapping into its own allocator class
body:
PR #45567: [XLA:GPU] Split command buffer VA remapping into its own allocator class

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45567

## 📝 Summary of Changes

This PR separates the command-buffer virtual-address remapping implementation from `GpuExecutableBufferAllocator` into a dedicated `GpuExecutableVaRemapAllocator` subclass. It is a structural refactor of the existing `SKIP_TEMP` behavior; no functional change is intended.

- `GpuExecutableBufferAllocator` is now the common base implementation for allocation resolution and the `ALWAYS_UPDATE` policy. It also remains the runtime fallback for `SKIP_TEMP` when VA remapping is unavailable.
- `ExecutionScope` is now polymorphic and is returned as `std::unique_ptr<ExecutionScope>`. Protected hooks such as `PrepareReservation` and `AllocateTransientBuffer` provide the extension points needed by address-policy-specific subclasses.
- The new `GpuExecutableVaRemapAllocator` owns the `SKIP_TEMP` implementation:
  - per-executor remapping state and synchronization;
  - deterministic VA reservation sizing and layout;
  - VMM-backed allocation of command-buffer-referenced temporary buffers;
  - persistent allocation indices combining constants with VA-remapped temporary allocations; and
  - synchronization of pending VMM operations during allocator teardown.
- `GpuExecutableBufferAllocator::Create` selects the base allocator for `ALWAYS_UPDATE` and the VA-remapping subclass for `SKIP_TEMP`.
- GPU executable and PJRT call sites now use the factory and pointer-owned execution scopes.
- The BUILD target includes the new source/header pair and retains the direct dependencies required by both implementations.
- VMM test logging now enables both allocator translation units so existing assertions continue to observe the VA-reservation messages after the code move.

This PR is stacked on #45130, **[XLA:GPU] Update command buffers when allocation policy changes**. The follow-up policy is implemented separately in #45568.

## 🎯 Justification

The base allocator previously mixed general buffer-allocation mechanics with one specific VMM address-stability policy. Splitting those responsibilities makes the default path easier to reason about and gives additional update policies a narrow place to implement reservation, allocation, and execution behavior without further expanding the base class.

This cleanup is primarily preparation for profiled command-buffer allocation policies. Existing GPU command-buffer workloads should retain the same `ALWAYS_UPDATE` and `SKIP_TEMP` behavior.

## 🚀 Kind of Contribution

♻️ Cleanup

## 📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)

Not applicable. This is a behavior-preserving refactor and makes no performance claim.

## 🧪 Unit Tests:

- Updated `GpuExecutableTest.CommandBufferAllocationPolicy` to construct allocators through the new factory and exercise the pointer-owned `ExecutionScope`.
- Existing assertions continue to cover the persistent-allocation sets for `ALWAYS_UPDATE` and `SKIP_TEMP`, including the non-VMM fallback path.

## 🧪 Execution Tests:

- Existing `VmmTest` command-buffer tests continue to cover the two-GEMM `SKIP_TEMP` path, VA reservation reuse, and fallback when the configured allocator does not provide VMM remapping.
- `ScopedBufferAllocatorVLog` now captures logs from `gpu_executable_va_remap_allocator.cc`, preserving the execution-test assertions whose log statements moved with the implementation.

title: Support shaped types in SimplifyArithPass
body:
Support shaped types in SimplifyArithPass

Originally the pass was written for the Fusion Emitters pipeline. Now that it
is also used for CPU block codegen, we can have shaped types as well.

This change updates SimplifyArithPass to handle shaped types (vectors and
tensors) safely across several rewrite patterns:
- In FindNarrowestValueInChain, use mlir::getElementTypeOrSelf to get the
  element type before querying bitwidths. Direct calls to
  Type::getIntOrFloatBitWidth() on ShapedType failed an MLIR assertion.
- In RewriteMinMaxFWithNaNPropagation and RewriteCmpI, construct
  DenseElementsAttr constants when operating on ShapedType operands.
- Add lit tests for shaped types and scalar NaN propagation mode in
  SimplifyArithPass.

title: The API goldens now include dunder methods defined in TensorFlow
body:
The API goldens now include dunder methods defined in TensorFlow

This allows using the goldens to generate more accurate type stubs, where
e.g. `tf.Tensor` supports binary operators and `tf.named_scope` is a context
manager.

I had to also fix two issues uncovered by this change

* `tf.Tensor` dunder methods don't always use `self`, so the name-based
  `staticmethod` heuristic added earlier misfired. I moved
  classmethod/staticmethod detection to the API generator, where we
  have access to the runtime objects.
* pybind11 docstring parsing didn't support *args, which led to
  `__exit__` having the wrong signature for some types.
* `__round__` is monkey-patched into `tf.Tensor` at import time by NumPy
  "behavior" internals, so we exclude it from the API to keep the API
  generation independent from import side-effects.

title: [XLA:GPU] Refactor DotMerger to use DotOperandDims and ShapeTracker.
body:
[XLA:GPU] Refactor DotMerger to use DotOperandDims and ShapeTracker.

This change enhances the capabilities of the DotMerger pass. Instead of relying on specific patterns like DotDecomposer's normal form, the new implementation uses `DotOperandDims` to track and categorize dimensions (Batch, Contracting, NonContracting) and `ShapeTracker` to generate the necessary transformation instructions (transpose, reshape, bitcast) to align operand shapes for merging.

Key improvements include:
-   Support for merging dots with different layouts on the shared or concatenated operands.
-   Ability to handle dots with arbitrary batch, contracting, and non-contracting dimension orders.
-   Merging of dots even when the non-shared operands have multiple non-contracting dimensions.
-   Improved handling of dependencies by merging only mutually unreachable dots within an equivalence class.
-   Simplification of consumer chains (transposes, reshapes, bitcasts) after the merged dot's output is sliced.

The equivalence classes are now built based on the shared operand's source instruction and the categorized dimensions at that source, allowing for more flexible grouping. The merging process involves transforming the operands to a common shape/layout before concatenation and then creating a single large dot. The results are then sliced and potentially transformed back to match the original dot outputs.

title: fix complex dtype byte-swap overrun in ByteSwapBuffer
body:
ByteSwapBuffer computes the number of components to swap, then ByteSwapArray walks that many words in place. On the num_of_elem == -1 path the count comes from the byte size: array_len = size / bytes_per_elem, where bytes_per_elem is the 4- or 8-byte component size, so array_len already counts every component in the buffer. For DT_COMPLEX64/DT_COMPLEX128 the code then does array_len *= 2, so ByteSwapArray swaps twice as many words as the buffer holds and reads/writes size bytes past the end. This path is taken when a cross-endian SavedModel or GraphDef is loaded on a big-endian host (ByteSwapTensorContentInNode, and the public ByteSwapTensorProto), where the dtype and tensor_content length come straight from the file, so a complex Const overruns the copy buffer.

Only double the count on the num_of_elem branch, where it is an element count that has to become a component count; the size-derived branch is already the component count. The sibling ByteSwapTensor path (which passes t->NumElements()) confirms the intended arithmetic. Added a regression test that runs ByteSwapTensorProto over both complex dtypes and checks the content round-trips without overrunning.

title: PR #44403: [XLA:CPU] onednn_threadpool: cap num_workers at n in parallel_for
body:
PR #44403: [XLA:CPU] onednn_threadpool: cap num_workers at n in parallel_for

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/44403

📝 Summary of Changes
`OneDnnThreadPool::parallel_for` (xla/backends/cpu/runtime/onednn/onednn_threadpool.h)  was passing `thread_pool_- NumThreads()` as `num_workers` regardless of `n`. Before   #42581, `Worker::Parallelize` had an entry-point clamp (`num_workers = std::min(num_work_items, num_workers)`) that silently fixed this up. #42581 replaced that clamp with a branch that triggers when `num_workers > num_work_items`:

  ```cpp
  if (num_workers > num_work_items) {
    num_partitions = ceil(num_work_items / 8);
    num_workers   = std::min(num_workers, num_partitions);
  }
  ```

  For oneDNN's small-n dispatches (reorders, packing, eltwise/softmax tiles), this collapses parallelism to ceil(n/8) cores. 
  eg: On a 56-thread host, n = 20 drops from 20 active cores to 3; n <= 8 falls through to a fully serial fallback. Multiplied across the many small primitives, this causes significant regression across multiple models when built with `build_with_onednn_async=true` and `XLA_FLAGS=--xla_cpu_experimental_onednn_custom_call=true`

  Fix
  Cap num_workers at n at the caller, matching the pattern already used in xla/backends/cpu/runtime/kernel.cc and xla/backends/cpu/runtime/convolution_lib.h: 
  ```cpp
  const size_t num_workers = std::min<size_t>(static_cast<size_t>(n),
                                              thread_pool_->NumThreads());
  ```

  With num_workers <= num_work_items, the call takes the else branch (num_partitions = num_workers) and behaves like pre-#42581. For n >= NumThreads(), the cap is a no-op and the heap/cacheline win from #42581 is fully preserved.


🎯 Justification
It fixes the significant regression (25%-60%) across multiple models run on CPU with onednn

title: [PjRt-IFRT] Reject XLA HloShardingV3 (NamedSharding) format in IFRT `HloShardingSerDes` serialization
body:
[PjRt-IFRT] Reject XLA HloShardingV3 (NamedSharding) format in IFRT `HloShardingSerDes` serialization

XLA `HloShardingV3` (NamedSharding) format is currently not version compatible across IFRT SerDes versions as the version compatibility contract has not been established around `HloShardingV3`, and `HloShardingV3` is intended to be used within the local XLA compiler. Allowing `HloShardingSerDes` to serialize `HloShardingV3` format can cause potential compatibility errors when communicating across different binary versions or using persistent artifacts such as model exports.

This change updates `HloShardingSerDes::Serialize` to explicitly reject `HloSharding` containing `HloShardingV3` format, returning an `InvalidArgumentError`.

title: [XLA:BF16_PROP] Do not propagate precision across element-type-converting bitcasts and protect bitcast operands
body:
[XLA:BF16_PROP] Do not propagate precision across element-type-converting bitcasts and protect bitcast operands

Fixes an infinite loop in BFloat16Propagation::ResolveInconsistencyOfAliasingBuffersHelper across bitcast instructions with mismatched input/output element types (e.g. bf16 <-> f32 or u32 <-> f32). Specifically:
- BFloat16Propagation::ShouldKeepPrecisionUnchanged returns true for HloOpcode::kBitcast when the input element type differs from the output element type.
- AllUsersConsumeBF16 returns true when checking a user instruction that is an HloOpcode::kBitcast whose operand expects BF16.
- Ensure only F32 values (value->shape().element_type() == F32) are inserted into values_that_must_be_kept_as_f32_ in DetermineInstructionPrecision and AdjustCalledComputationRoot, preventing F32 bitcast roots from marking aliased native BF16 operands as requiring F32.

title: PR #45130: [XLA:GPU] Trigger command buffers update when persistent allocations set changed.
body:
PR #45130: [XLA:GPU] Trigger command buffers update when persistent allocations set changed.

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45130

For command buffer run, add the required processing for allowing `persistent_alloc_indices` to transition only from absent to present across execution steps and must remain unchanged once present. 

We may require this transition because the chosen of buffer allocations whose address are in `persistent_alloc_indices` might not be available from the first step, e.g, if persistent allocations are only available after several steps of profiling.  So we need to make sure that command buffer is correctly updated when `persistent_alloc_indices` is changed across steps. 


📝 Summary of Changes

- Document that `persistent_alloc_indices` may transition only from absent to
  present across execution steps and must remain unchanged once present.
- Track only whether persistent-allocation information was valid when each
  executor's command buffer was recorded, avoiding an owned vector copy and
  repeated value comparisons.
- Force a full command-buffer update in `CommandBufferThunk::Initialize` when
  persistent allocation information first becomes valid.
- In `ExecuteOnStream`, recover from a recorded/current information-validity
  mismatch by fully updating the command buffer. This covers a
  profiling-skipped update and interleaving with an older execution initialized
  before policy activation.
- Use the public `ShapedSlice` header and its direct BUILD dependency.

🎯 Justification

The persistent allocation policy controls which recorded addresses a command
buffer can safely retain. When the policy first becomes available, an
allocation-filtered update can skip a command whose allocations are now all
persistent, leaving stale addresses in the command buffer. A full update fixes
that transition.

Although the policy transition is logically one-way, executions initialized on
opposite sides of it can interleave on the shared per-executor command buffer.
An Execute-time validity check therefore forces a full update for either
recorded/current mismatch without comparing policy vectors on every step.

🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix

📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)

N/A. This is a correctness fix.

🧪 Unit Tests:

Extended `PersistentAllocIndicesBecomingAvailableTriggersUpdate` to verify:

- absent-to-present activation during Initialize triggers exactly one update;
- Execute recovers when the initialization update was skipped;
- an older absent-policy execution and the following present-policy execution
  each restore the correct recorded addresses when they interleave.

Also ran `GpuExecutableTest.CommandBufferAllocationPolicy`.

🧪 Execution Tests:

Ran the focused command-buffer regression and allocation-policy test with
Bazel. All seven configured GPU architecture variants of
`command_buffer_thunk_test` passed, and `gpu_executable_test` passed.

author: harche
commit_messages:
['KEP-6063: Implement per-pod PID limit (Alpha)

Add support for per-pod PID limits via spec.resources.limits.pids,
gated behind the PerPodPIDLimit feature gate (Alpha, disabled by default).
The kubelet enforces the effective limit as min(node podPidsLimit, pod pids limit)
on cgroupsv2 nodes, with admission rejection on cgroupsv1. A PIDLimitCapped
warning event is emitted when the pod requested limit exceeds the node podPidsLimit.

- Add PerPodPIDLimit feature gate (Alpha, v1.37)
- Register pids as a standard, integer resource
- Validate pids values in the range 128-16384; reject requests.pids
- Add PodValidationOptions-based feature gate check for pids resource
- Add kubelet admission check for cgroupsv2 requirement
- Add Node Declared Features support for PerPodPIDLimit
- Add unit tests for validation, helpers, kubelet logic, eviction
- Add e2e node tests for PID limit enforcement, capping, PSA, hostPID, static pods
- Add PID to supportedPodLevelResources with generic LimitOnly defaulting skip

Additional hardening for the limit-only pod-level resource semantics:

- Exclude limit-only resources (pids) from IsPodLevelResourcesSet (both
  copies) so a pids-only pod keeps its container-derived QOS class and
  does not switch quota, cpumanager/memorymanager, or kuberuntime callers
  onto pod-level resource code paths
- Skip pod-level request/hugepage-limit defaulting (v1 and internal) when
  the only pod-level entries are limit-only resources, preventing
  materialized pod-level cpu/memory requests (QOS drift) and hugepage
  limits that would fail the "HugePages require cpu or memory" validation
- Exclude limit-only resources from PodRequests/PodLimits aggregation
- Reject pids in LimitRange validation for all limit types
- Depend PerPodPIDLimit on PodLevelResourcesFixKubeletQOSClass to keep the
  legacy pod-level QOS derivation path from misclassifying pids-only pods
- Fail closed at kubelet admission when the gate is disabled or the value
  is out of range (static pods bypass apiserver validation), mirroring
  isPodLevelResourcesSupported; Windows/unsupported platforms always reject
- Emit PIDLimitCapped only after the pod cgroup is successfully created
- Remove unused NDF StaticConfiguration.Cgroupsv2 plumbing
- Rewrite event unit tests to exercise EnsureExists; add tests for update
  ratcheting, internal defaulting, quota constraint enforcement, fractional
  values, aggregation semantics, admission (linux/windows), QOS regression,
  and e2e assertions for QOS class and the PIDLimitCapped event

Signed-off-by: BhargaviGudi <bgudi@redhat.com>
Signed-off-by: Harshal Patil <harpatil@redhat.com>']

#### What type of PR is this?

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

Introduces the Kubelet endpoint for surfacing allocated pod information. This endpoint will be used to provide the `/allocated` pod subresource in a later release.

---

The `/allocated` subresource was originally proposed as part of the (not yet merged) [Dynamic Containers KEP](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/6169):

> #### Allocated Subresource
> 
> A new read-only `/allocated` subresource on pods will surface the allocated pod spec. The allocated
> pod will be fetched directly from the Kubelet on-demand, thus avoiding additional storage overhead
> in the API server.
> 
> The Kubelet will serve a new `/allocatedPods` endpoint that functions similarly to `/pods` and
> `/runningPods`, and returns a list of all the allocated pods on the node. An allocated pod is
> represented as a `v1.Pod` object, but the status field is left blank. The subpath
> `/allocatedPods/<POD UID>` can be used to fetch an individual allocated pod, which is what the API
> server will use to serve the allocated pod subresource.
> 
> **Justification:** The desired pod spec (stored in the pod resource) can diverge from the allocated
> pod spec (stored locally by the Kubelet) for an arbitrary amount of time. For in-place resize, this
> was handled by surfacing allocated resources in the pod status. This KEP (and the expected follow
> ups) significantly increases the API surface of the mutable / allocatable portion of the Pod spec,
> and simply mirroring these fields into the pod status will drastically inflate the size of the pod
> object. Similarly, duplicating every pod into an `AllocatedPod` object would heavily inflate the API
> server object count and data size.

We realized that this subresource can also let us simplify a feature that is landing in v1.37, https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/139425

So, this PR is pulling this feature into v1.37.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/6030

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

This PR was forked from https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/140659 to get the Kubelet piece into v1.37, since we were API reviewer constrained. Changes from that PR include:

1. Renamed the feature gate to be Kubelet specific (`PodAllocatedSubresource` --> `KubeletAllocatedPodsEndpoint`)
2. Changed the Kubelet endpoint path to be consistent with other pod-specific endpoints (`/allocatedPods/namespace/name(/uid)` with optional UID, rather than `/allocatedPods/UID`). This required some small changes to the interfaces and tests to fetch pods by name instead of UID.
3. Drop the API changes & integration test
4. Use the node proxy subresource to query the Kubelet endpoint directly in the E2E test.

This PR was written with assistance from Antigravity with Gemini.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?
```release-note
A new `allocatedPods` kubelet endpoint surfaces the Kubelet's allocated pod spec. This can be used to debug in-place pod resizing and other issues with pod updates. Requires the `KubeletAllocatedPodsEndpoint` FeatureGate.
```

/sig node
/milestone v1.37

title: kubelet: fix flaky kuberuntime manager unit test
body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind flake

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

Fixes a unit test flake in `TestComputePodActionsWithInitContainers` (which also caused
`TestComputePodActionsWithInitAndEphemeralContainers` to fail since it re-runs the init container
test suite).

The test start flaking after https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/140846, where commit f8f9d0571e9db4a3937b3f5fa4da0a567fa24f83 being the commit that introduced the flake.

The test suite shared a single `kubeGenericRuntimeManager` instance across all subtests in the
table test. Inside each subtest, `InitializeActuatedPod` checks if pod resource state is already
cached in `actuatedState`. Because every subtest uses the exact same pod UID, only the first subtest
to run actually populated the cache—subsequent subtests hit the early return guard and skipped
initialization, inheriting leftover state from whichever test ran before them. 

Since Go map iteration order is randomized, this caused intermittent failures whenever a subtest
ran after one that modified container resources.

Moving `createTestRuntimeManager` inside `t.Run` ensures every subtest gets its own isolated
manager and clean state.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/pr-logs/pull/140244/pull-kubernetes-unit/2079889038847774720

title: Skip Unused condition evaluation for unbound PVCs
body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug
/sig storage

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

The PVC protection controller evaluates the `Unused` condition (gated by the `PersistentVolumeClaimUnusedSinceTime` feature) and writes it to the PVC status. During initial binding, this write races with the PV binder's `bindClaimToVolume`, which also updates the same PVC. The two writers collide and produce 409 Conflict errors, causing wasted retries on both controllers during the busy binding phase.

This PR skips the `Unused` condition evaluation until the PVC is `Bound`. Once the claim is bound, the PV binder is finished writing it, so the protection controller can safely own the condition without contending with the binder. An unbound PVC is not in use by any pod anyway, so deferring the evaluation has no functional downside.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

N/A

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

/cc @arvindparekh @gnufied

This fixes a binding-time conflict in the `Unused` condition introduced by KEP-5541. It was discovered during development of #140721. We measured up to 15% of the PVCs receiving a 409 Conflict error during a benchmark.

`PersistentVolumeClaimUnusedSinceTime` is Alpha in 1.36 (off by default) and Beta in 1.37 (on by default), so this only affects clusters with the feature enabled.

Since this is a slight behavior change to the `Unused` condition, it would be ideal to land it before the 1.37 release, so the "evaluate only once bound" semantics ship as part of the initial Beta (on-by-default) rollout rather than changing behavior in a later release.

Unit tests in `pvc_protection_controller_test.go` are updated: a new `bound()` helper marks the PVC as `ClaimBound` in the existing feature-enabled cases, plus a new case asserts that a pending (unbound) PVC produces no pod list and no status update.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
Fixed 409 Conflict errors between the PVC protection controller and the PV binder during initial PVC binding. The `Unused` condition is now evaluated only after the PVC is bound.
```

#### Additional documentation e.g., KEPs (Kubernetes Enhancement Proposals), usage docs, etc.:

```docs
- [KEP-5541] (Report Last Used Time On a PVC): https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/blob/45f8bae48eb69f8aab2f6d5a9ef55d4a2675f3d7/keps/sig-storage/5541-pvc-last-used-time-status-field/README.md
```

#### What this PR does / why we need it:
Fixes a scheduler panic caused by incorrect argument ordering in `CompositePodGroup` event handlers.
Previously, the `addCompositePodGroup` and `updateCompositePodGroup` handlers were passing arguments in the wrong order or providing `nil` incorrectly to `MoveAllToActiveOrBackoffQueue` (e.g., passing `(newObj, oldObj)` or `(cpg, nil)` instead of `(nil, cpg)` for Add events). This PR:
1. Corrects the argument ordering to adhere to the standard `(oldObj, newObj)` convention.
2. Refactors `TestAddCompositePodGroup` and `TestUpdateCompositePodGroup` to utilize the real plugin `QueueingHint` logic. The test hook now correctly stages the test Pod and its hierarchical groups in the queue so the hints evaluate successfully, ensuring the correct order of arguments passed to QueueingHint functions.

title: Promote AllowUnsafeMalformedObjectDeletion to beta
body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind feature

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

Promotes `AllowUnsafeMalformedObjectDeletion` to beta as planned in KEP-3926.

The second commit fixes a side effect of enabling the gate by default: LIST decode failures now go through the corrupt object deleter, which replaced the underlying cause with a generic `failed to read one or more ... from the storage` message. The watch cache flattens errors to their message text, so the status causes are lost on that path and a broken CRD conversion webhook becomes hard to diagnose. The message now carries the first underlying error as an indicator for the root cause. Caught by `TestWebhookConverterWithWatchCache` in [pull-kubernetes-integration](https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/pr-logs/pull/140785/pull-kubernetes-integration/2079572982832828416).

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:

xref kubernetes/enhancements#3926

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
The AllowUnsafeMalformedObjectDeletion feature is now beta and enabled by default. List errors for objects that cannot be read from the storage now include the first underlying cause in the error message.
```

title: e2e_node: add CRI container metrics test for PodAndContainerStatsFromCRI
body:
## What type of PR is this?

/kind feature
/sig node
/area kubelet

## What this PR does / why we need it:

Adds an e2e_node test that validates the `/metrics/cadvisor` endpoint reports
correct container metrics when the `PodAndContainerStatsFromCRI` feature gate
is enabled. This exercises the CRI metrics collection path where container stats
are fetched from the runtime via `ListPodSandboxMetrics` instead of cadvisor.

The test validates:
- Per-container CPU, memory, filesystem, and process metrics
- Pod-level network metrics (reported on the sandbox)
- `kubelet_metrics_provider` metric reports `provider=cri`

This test complements the existing `ContainerMetrics` test
(`container_metrics_test.go`) which validates the cadvisor path and skips
when `PodAndContainerStatsFromCRI` is enabled. The CRI test mirrors its
structure, reusing the same helper functions (`createMetricsPods`,
`appendMatchesForContainer`, `getContainerMetrics`).

## Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

KEP: kubernetes/enhancements#2371
Depends on: #140780

## Special notes for your reviewer:

This test depends on #140780 which adds `namespace`, `pod`, and `container`
labels to the CRI metrics collector. Without that fix, the CRI path only
exposes `id`, `name`, and `image` labels from the runtime, which would cause
the shared `containerID()` helper to fail to match metrics to pods.

Some metrics that are required in the cadvisor path are optional here because
CRI-O may not always report them (e.g., blkio metrics depend on kernel/runtime
support, `container_memory_failcnt` is cgroup v1 only).

The `Eventually` timeout is 3 minutes (vs 1 minute in the cadvisor test) to
account for CRI-O needing time to accumulate container statistics after pod
creation.

## Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
NONE
```

## Additional documentation e.g., KEPs (Kubernetes Enhancement Proposals), usage docs, etc.:

KEP: https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/2371

UPSTREAM: <carry>: provide a new admission plugin to mutate management pods CPUs requests

The ManagementCPUOverride admission plugin replaces pod container CPU requests with a new management resource.
It applies to all pods that:
 1. are in an allowed namespace
 2. and have the workload annotation.

It also sets the new management resource request and limit and  set resource annotation that CRI-O can
recognize and apply the relevant changes.
For more information, see - https://github.com/openshift/enhancements/pull/703

Conditions for CPUs requests deletion:
 1. The namespace should have allowed annotation "workload.openshift.io/allowed": "management"
 2. The pod should have management annotation: "workload.openshift.io/management": "{"effect": "PreferredDuringScheduling"}"
 3. All nodes under the cluster should have new management resource - "management.workload.openshift.io/cores"
 4. The CPU request deletion will not change the pod QoS class

UPSTREAM: <carry>: Fix conformance and serial tests by stopping node cordoning

Master nodes already have `master` taint which
cannot be tolerated by normal workloads. If we manually
cordon the master nodes again, some of the control plane
components cannot get rescheduled unless they have
toleration to the `node.kubernetes.io/unschedulable`
taint. Even if we have the toleration in the pod
spec, because of the backwards compability issues
scheduler will ignore nodes which have `unschedulable`
field set. IOW:

- Cordoning master nodes is redundant as masters already
  have taints
- Cordoning master nodes can cause issues which are hard
  to debug as control-plane components may be evicted/preempted
  during e2e run(highly unlikely but a possibility).

So, let's stop cordoning master nodes.

title: kubelet: add namespace/pod/container labels to CRI metrics collector
body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind feature

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

When the PodAndContainerStatsFromCRI feature gate is enabled, the
/metrics/cadvisor endpoint uses the CRI metrics collector which passes
through the CRI runtime's metric labels verbatim. CRI runtimes like
CRI-O only provide id, name, and image labels — they do not include
the Kubernetes-level namespace, pod, and container labels that
monitoring tooling expects.

This PR resolves this by calling ListPodSandbox and ListContainers at
scrape time to build ID-to-metadata maps, then appending namespace,
pod, and container labels to each metric. This follows the same pattern
that criStatsProvider.getPodAndContainerMaps already uses for
/stats/summary.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

KEP: https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/2371
Fixes https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/140778

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

An alternative approach that would avoid the 2 extra RPC calls per scrape is documented in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/140778.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note

```

title: Automated cherry pick of #140437: DRA: skip the counter check for a persisted shared device
body:
Cherry pick of #140437 on release-1.36.

#140437: DRA: skip the counter check for a persisted shared device

/kind bug
/priority important-soon
/sig node
/wg device-management

#### What this PR does / why we need it

This backports the persisted shared-device counter-accounting fix from #140437 to `release-1.36`.

When a device both allows multiple allocations (`DRAConsumableCapacity`) and consumes shared counters (`DRAPartitionableDevices`), an existing allocation may be persisted with a `ShareID` but no `ConsumedCapacity`. In that case the device is present in `AllocatedSharedDeviceIDs` but has no entry in `AggregatedCapacity`.

Counter availability is reconstructed through `IsDeviceAllocated`, which already recognizes `AllocatedSharedDeviceIDs`, so the persisted device has its counters subtracted from the available counter pool. However `deviceCapacityInUse`, which decides whether an allow-multiple device should skip the counter check, only recognizes `AggregatedCapacity` and capacity reserved during the current allocation search.

As a result, a later claim sharing the same device can charge the device's physical counters a second time and be rejected with a false `Insufficient counters` result, leaving an otherwise schedulable pod pending.

This change makes `deviceCapacityInUse` also recognize persisted shares in `AllocatedSharedDeviceIDs`, matching the persisted-state semantics already used by `IsDeviceAllocated`. It applies to the incubating and experimental allocators. The stable allocator does not support `ConsumableCapacity` and is unaffected.

`DRAConsumableCapacity` and `DRAPartitionableDevices` are both beta and enabled by default in Kubernetes 1.36, and the affected incubating allocator is selected by the default feature configuration, so the issue is reachable on a default 1.36 cluster.

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes

Backport of #140437. The master-side change resolved #140433.

#### Special notes for your reviewer

This is intentionally a narrow backport of the single master commit `acf342bdcaba4c5ac3489e4c41394ba683a315f7`.

The backport changes exactly three files: the shared allocator regression-test table, the incubating allocator, and the experimental allocator.

The production change keeps every existing form of the in-use check: persisted aggregated capacity, a persisted shared allocation recorded only by `ShareID`, and capacity reserved during the current allocation search. The lookup compares the underlying `DeviceID`, so a persisted share of another device cannot cause this device's counter check to be skipped.

The implementation scans `AllocatedSharedDeviceIDs` rather than introducing a second precomputed `Set[DeviceID]`. This matches the existing `IsDeviceAllocated` approach and avoids a second copy of persisted shared-device state. The scan is limited to allow-multiple candidates; a derived index can be considered separately if profiling shows this lookup to be significant.

Only `release-1.36` is targeted. The bug requires both `DRAConsumableCapacity` and `DRAPartitionableDevices`; these are beta and on by default in 1.36 but alpha and off by default in 1.35 and earlier, so the issue is not reachable by default on the older supported release branches and a backport there is not warranted under the cherry-pick policy.

The scope is limited to the double-count of a persisted allow-multiple share. It does not change how a device that already carries a persisted share is handled if it is later requested as a dedicated allocation; that is a separate correctness question, left as a follow-up on master rather than widened into this backport.

The related rollback fix from #140431 is already in `release-1.36` via #140663. That one addresses state leaked during rejection and backtracking within a single allocation search, whereas this PR addresses persisted shared state reconstructed across scheduling cycles. The two are related but independent.

The PoolID counter-cache fix from #140435 is being backported separately in #140504. It is not a prerequisite for this change, and keeping the two fixes in separate PRs preserves narrow review and rollback boundaries.

#### Validation

Validated locally against `release-1.36` (go1.26, workspace mode):

- [x] `git diff --check` is clean, and the changed-file set is exactly the shared allocator test file plus the incubating and experimental allocator files (`+62/-6`).
- [x] `go test ./structured/... -run 'TestAllocator/partitionable-consumable-capacity-shared-device-counter-not-recharged'` passes on the incubating and experimental allocators.
- [x] `go test -race ./structured/...` passes.
- [x] `go test ./structured/... -count=10` passes across 10 repetitions.
- [x] With the regression test kept and the two production hunks temporarily reverted to their `release-1.36` versions, the targeted test fails on the incubating allocator with `Insufficient counters device="driver-a/pool-1/device-1"`.
- [x] With the production fix restored, the targeted test passes.

Happy to re-run any additional branch-specific validation the release team prefers.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
Fixed a DRA consumable-capacity scheduling bug: a device that consumes shared counters could have them counted twice when it already had a persisted shared allocation with no consumed capacity, wrongly rejecting a later claim for the same device and leaving the pod pending.
```

title: DRA: fail All requests when a matching device is capacity-exhausted
body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

Fixes structured DRA allocator behavior for `allocationMode: All` with consumable capacity (`DRAConsumableCapacity`).

Per `CapacityRequirements` godoc, an All request must fail when a device otherwise matches the request and advertises sufficient static capacity, but cannot be allocated (for example, because remaining capacity is exhausted on a multi-alloc device).

When gathering devices for All, the allocator incorrectly used `alloc.CmpRequestOverCapacity`, which includes pre-consumed remaining capacity. Capacity-exhausted matching devices were filtered out of `allDevices`, so All
could succeed with only the still-free subset.

##### Example
Two multi-alloc devices each with `capacity0=1`; device-1 is fully consumed by another allocation. An All request for `capacity0=1` must fail, not return device-2 alone.

The fix uses a static-capacity-only check at All gather time (empty consumed state). Remaining capacity continues to be enforced in `allocateDevice`, so a blocked matching device causes the whole All request to fail, consistent with
exclusive in-use devices, which were already handled correctly.

Also reverts the `consumable-capacity-multi-allocatable-device-allocation-mode-all-in-use-insufficient` allocator table case to expect no allocation. That case originally expected failure (KEP 5075) and was later flipped to partial success alongside an ExactCount multi-device fix.

```yaml
apiVersion: resource.k8s.io/v1
kind: ResourceClaim
metadata:
  name: all-gpus
spec:
  devices:
    requests:
    - name: req0
      exactly:
        allocationMode: All
        deviceClassName: gpu-class
        capacity:
          requests:
            memory: 4Gi
```

If another pod already consumed all capacity on one matching device, the claim must stay unallocated rather than succeeding with the remaining device(s) only.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

N/A

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

- Change is limited to All-mode gather in experimental and incubating allocators.
- Other All+capacity table cases are unchanged (`filter-out-*`, `in-use-sufficient`, `allocating-insufficient`).
- Requires `DRAConsumableCapacity`.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
Fixed a bug where ResourceClaims using `allocationMode: All` with consumable capacity could be partially allocated when a matching device had insufficient remaining capacity. Such claims now correctly fail to allocate until all matching devices can be satisfied.
```

#### Additional documentation e.g., KEPs (Kubernetes Enhancement Proposals), usage docs, etc.:

```docs

```

title: cli-runtime: include group in resource-not-found error message
body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

`kubectl` drops the group name from the error when a resource type is requested with a group qualifier it doesn't belong to. For example, `kubectl get pdb.hpa` prints `the server doesn't have a resource type "pdb"`, which is wrong. `pdb` exists, it just doesn't exist in the `hpa` group. The error reads as if the resource type itself is unknown, when the real problem is the group.

```
$ kubectl get pdb.hpa
error: the server doesn't have a resource type "pdb"
```
This PR includes the group in the error message when one is present, so the same command now reports 
```
the server doesn't have a resource type "pdb" in group "hpa"`.
```

Root cause: in `staging/src/k8s.io/cli-runtime/pkg/resource/builder.go`, `mappingFor` parses the resource arg into a `schema.GroupResource{Resource, Group}`, but on a `NoMatchError` builds the error from `.Resource` only, discarding `.Group`.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubectl/issues/1865

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

Added `TestNoSelectorUnknownResourceTypeWithGroup` in `builder_test.go` covering the group case, alongside the existing `TestNoSelectorUnknowResourceType`.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
kubectl now includes the group name in the error message when a resource type is not found under the specified group, e.g. "the server doesn't have a resource type \"pdb\" in group \"hpa\"".
```

```docs

title: Update google.golang.org/grpc to v1.82.1
body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind dependency

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

This updates google.golang.org/grpc from v1.81.1 to v1.82.1. Upstream published v1.82.1 as a security release. It fixes three issues.

- A gRPC server now stops reading from a connection when a peer sends too many HTTP/2 control frames. Before this change, a peer could flood a server with control frames and make it use too much memory and CPU. See grpc/grpc-go#9236. There is no fixed v1.81.x release.
- The GRPC_GO_EXPERIMENTAL_DISABLE_STRICT_PATH_CHECKING environment variable is removed. Setting it turned strict path checking off and brought back the authorization bypass from CVE-2026-33186.
- The old gzip Decompressor API now limits how much data it decompresses, so a small compressed message can no longer use an unbounded amount of memory. Kubernetes does not call this API.

The update does not change any other dependency. Kubernetes already requires newer versions of everything grpc v1.82.1 needs, so the vendor changes cover only vendor/google.golang.org/grpc.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

N/A

I ran the standard dependency workflow.

- `hack/pin-dependency.sh google.golang.org/grpc v1.82.1`
- `hack/update-vendor.sh`

- `hack/verify-typecheck.sh` passes on all platforms.

Updated google.golang.org/grpc to v1.82.1. This adds a server-side limit on HTTP/2 control frame flooding. It also removes the GRPC_GO_EXPERIMENTAL_DISABLE_STRICT_PATH_CHECKING environment variable, so strict path checking is now always on.

title: DRA: add more DistinctAttribute tests
body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind cleanup

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

Adds regression tests to the shared structured DRA allocator test suite (`TestAllocator`) for `DistinctAttribute` claim constraints when a single request allocates more than one device.

Background: `distinctAttributeConstraint` previously tracked each chosen device's attribute in a map keyed by request name. When a request allocated multiple devices (`count > 1`), each device overwrote the previous one, so the distinctness check only compared a candidate against the most recent device of that request. The allocator could return, for example, `[red, blue, red]` for a request requiring distinct values.

The code has since been fixed upstream (the constraint now tracks every chosen device in a slice rather than a map keyed by request name). However, the existing distinct-constraint tests only used `count=2`, which cannot trigger the
overwrite. This PR adds cases with `count>=3` and a multi-request constraint scope, for both scalar and list-type attributes, including positive controls, so the regression stays covered! 🟢 

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

N/A

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

Tests only; no production code changes. The cases require the `DRAConsumableCapacity` feature (and `DRAListTypeAttributes` for the list-type variants). They pass against the current slice-based `distinctAttributeConstraint` implementation and fail against the earlier map-keyed-by-request-name version.

request name: multiple devices from one request overwrote each other, so
the distinctness check only compared against the last-seen device and
accepted duplicate attribute values. Existing distinct-constraint tests
only used count=2, which cannot trigger the overwrite.']

title: kube-proxy/nftables: avoid numgen map for single-endpoint service DNAT
body:

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

Many maps in a nftables table seems to be costly when adding rules. Adding rules does a scan of every map in the existing ruleset, making it very expensive to do so.

To avoid having a ruleset with many maps, this PR allows services with single-endpoints to avoid using a map, in an attempt to decrease the number of maps in use.

an validation error returned separately if enabled. For consistency
the option for returning the GVK gets renamed.']

title: [WAS] KEP-6089: Support Composite PodGroup for Building blocks APIs and workloadbuilder
body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind feature

#### What this PR does / why we need it:
- Adds reusable building block struct types to `scheduling.k8s.io` for the CompositePodGroup
- Add supports for CompositePodGroup to `workloadbuilder` library
- Enforces the `WorkloadInput` leaf/composite union in both the build and validate phases: a composite node may not set leaf building blocks, and a leaf node may not set composite building blocks
- Enforces Workload-wide uniqueness of template names at build time so a materialized (Composite)PodGroup resolves unambiguously by name
- Aligns `Validate` well-formedness with `BuildWorkload`: empty item names are rejected in both phases, and update validation correlates old/new items level-by-level by name

<details><summary>Union validation flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  n["WorkloadInput (per node)"] --> q{composite?}
  q -->|yes| r{leaf block set?}
  q -->|no| s{composite block set?}
  r -->|yes| e1[error]
  s -->|yes| e2[error]
  r -->|no| ok[OK]
  s -->|no| ok
```
</details>

#### What type of PR is this?

<!--

/kind bug

/kind cleanup

Optionally add one or more of the following kinds if applicable:
/kind api-change
/kind deprecation
/kind failing-test
/kind flake
/kind regression
-->

/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

resource.Quantity embeds a pointer indirectly. Therefore, copying a Quantity value can copy the *inf.Dec pointer while preserving its reference to same mutable decimal object. Mutating copied Quantity may then mutate decimal value held by original Quantity.

```
  type Quantity struct {
      // Used when quantity fits in scaled int64 form.
      i int64Amount

      // Used for decimal representation.
      d infDecAmount

      s string
      Format
  }

  type infDecAmount struct {
      *inf.Dec
  }
```

  `CmpRequestOverCapacity()` operates on ConsumedCapacity, which stores pointers to resource.Quantity values:

```
  type ConsumedCapacity map[resourceapi.QualifiedName]*resource.Quantity
```

  `CmpRequestOverCapacity()` checks whether adding a new request to currently consumed device capacity remains within device capacity. It is intended to perform a temporary capacity calculation and must not modify scheduler state, ResourceClaim requests, or informer cache objects.

```
  func CmpRequestOverCapacity(...) {
      ...
      // Build temporary total capacity for this check.
      clone := currentConsumedCapacity.Clone()
      ...
      // calculateConsumedCapacity(): may return a shallow copy of requestedVal, retaining its internal *inf.Dec.
      consumedCapacity := calculateConsumedCapacity(requestedValPtr, cap) // line 42
      ...
      // Old code: created a new outer Quantity value, but could retain a shared internal *inf.Dec pointer.
      clone[name] = ptr.To(consumedCapacity)   // line 51
      // Fixed code: clone[name] = ptr.To(consumedCapacity.DeepCopy())
      ...
      if allocatingVal, allocatingFound := allocatingCapacity[name]; allocatingFound {
          // Add may mutate clone[name]'s internal *inf.Dec in place.
          clone[name].Add(*allocatingVal)  // line 55
      }
  }
```

In result, for large decimal requests, adding existing consumption can inflate cached ResourceClaim request values.
Within same scheduler process, later reads from informer cache may observe this inflated request value.


A new unit test proves the error of original code

```
  Expected
      <[]v1.AllocationResult | len:0, cap:0>: nil
  to consist of
      ... two DeviceRequestAllocationResult entries ...

  --- FAIL: TestAllocator/consumable-capacity-requests-are-not-modified
```
