title: Fix flaky skill watch test: add non-recursive watchers on skill subdirectories
body:
In `scan` mode, the `watch skill file changes` integration test flakily times out because content-only modifications to `SKILL.md` (two levels deep: `skillsDir/skill-name/SKILL.md`) are sometimes not detected on macOS CI VMs.

## Root cause

Skills were watched exclusively via a recursive `@parcel/watcher` on `skillsDir`. On macOS VMs, this recursive watcher can fail to fire for content-only changes deep in the tree. Agents don't have this problem because they use a non-recursive `fs.watch`/kqueue watcher on a directory whose direct children are the watched files.

## Fix

In `_scanRoot` for `DiscoveredType.Skill`, add an explicit **non-recursive** watcher on each discovered skill subdirectory (trigger = the `SKILL.md` file URI):

```typescript
// before: only recursive watcher on skillsDir
addWatch(watchRootUris, rootUri, root.recursive ?? false, rootUri);

// after: also add non-recursive watcher on each skill's subdirectory
addWatch(watchRootUris, child.resource, false, skillFile);
```

When `SKILL.md` is modified, `e.affects(skillFile)` returns `true` immediately — a more specific, reliable trigger that doesn't depend on `@parcel/watcher`'s recursive event delivery. This mirrors how `discover` mode watches individual skill file paths.

## Tests

- Updated `installs watchers for roots that contain discovered customizations` to assert skill subdirectories (e.g. `.github/skills/bar`) are now watched non-recursively in addition to the recursive `skillsDir` watcher.
- Added `fires onDidChange when an existing SKILL.md file is modified` to directly validate content-change detection via the new non-recursive watcher.

- Fixes #327447

title: Set AI_AGENT for all agent sessions, not just runInTerminal
body:
Fixes #326069

## What

`AI_AGENT` is a cross-vendor environment-variable convention that `git` and `gh` inherit, and which GitHub's data team uses to attribute downstream activity (commits, PRs) back to the AI surface that originated it. jolitz asked that every GitHub Copilot surface set a distinct value of the form `github_copilot_[SURFACE]`, and cwebster-99 clarified that the intent is to track **all** agent usage in VS Code, not just the CLI.

Before this change VS Code set `AI_AGENT` in exactly one place — the Local harness's `runInTerminal` tool — so every agent-host session was invisible to the metric.

This adds a single shared constant and sets the marker at every layer of the spawn chain, so the guarantee doesn't depend on one inheritance path staying intact.

New module `src/vs/platform/chat/common/aiAgentEnv.ts` exports `AiAgentEnvVar` / `AiAgentEnvValue` (`github_copilot_vscode_agent`), consumed by:

| File | Why it's needed here |
|---|---|
| `electronAgentHostStarter.ts` | root of the desktop agent-host spawn chain |
| `nodeAgentHostStarter.ts` | root of the server/remote chain |
| `copilotAgent.ts` | the CLI env is rebuilt from scratch and a strip loop deletes all `VSCODE_*`/`ELECTRON_*` keys, so it must be re-set afterwards |
| `claudeSdkOptions.ts` | the Claude SDK **replaces** the subprocess env rather than merging, and proxied (Copilot-routed) mode deliberately builds a sparse env — inheritance alone would drop it. Also set in `settings.env`, which the CLI layers onto Bash-tool commands |
| `codexLaunchConfig.ts` | Codex filters its shell tool's env through `shell_environment_policy`, so it also needs `-c shell_environment_policy.set.AI_AGENT=...` |
| `agentHostTerminalManager.ts` | AHP terminal pty env |
| `toolTerminalCreator.ts` | pre-existing Local-harness implementation, switched from a string literal to the shared constant (no behavior change) |

Single value for all harnesses (P1). Per-harness granularity (`github_copilot_vscode_agent_claude`, …) is deliberately deferred.

## Scenarios covered

- Agent host process itself (desktop + server/remote)
- Agent-host **Copilot CLI** sessions
- Agent-host **Codex** sessions
- Agent-host **Claude** sessions (partially — see caveat)
- Agent-host terminals (`chat.agentHost.customTerminalTool.enabled`)
- Local harness `runInTerminal` (unchanged behavior, now sharing the constant)

## Validation

Static: `typecheck-client`, `valid-layers-check`, `eslint` and `compile` are clean; 65 targeted unit tests pass.

Runtime, against a Code OSS build from these sources (Agents window). The probe has the agent run a script that writes the marker vars to a file, which is then read directly from disk rather than parsed out of the chat response:

| Surface | `AI_AGENT` observed by the agent's shell tool |
|---|---|
| Agent host utility process (`ps eww`) | `github_copilot_vscode_agent` |
| Copilot CLI subprocess (`ps eww`) | `github_copilot_vscode_agent` |
| **AH Copilot CLI** shell tool | `github_copilot_vscode_agent` |
| **AH Codex** shell tool | `github_copilot_vscode_agent` |
| **AH Claude** bash tool | `claude-code_<version>_agent` (see caveat) |

Additionally:

- Reproduced the full Copilot stdio path standalone (`CopilotClient` + `RuntimeConnection.forStdio`) and confirmed the marker survives **with** MXC sandbox auto-detection (`MXC_BIN_DIR`) and **with** a `sandboxConfig` pushed via `session.rpc.options.update`.
- Verified the new Codex `-c` argument against the real `codex` binary (`codex-cli 0.142.0`) via `codex sandbox`: the key is accepted, is genuinely necessary (an `inherit = "core"` policy strips an inherited `AI_AGENT`), and it **merges into** rather than clobbers a user's existing `shell_environment_policy.set` table.

## Caveats

1. **Claude re-stamps the variable for its own bash tool.** The bundled `claude` binary overwrites `AI_AGENT` with `claude-code_<version>_agent` when it invokes its agent bash tool. Our value is present in the Claude process and in everything else it spawns, but Claude's bash tool asserts its own vendor marker. This is not overridable from VS Code by setting env alone and would need an upstream change.
2. **The extension-host Copilot CLI harness is not covered.** That harness is being deprecated in favor of the agent-host one, so no change was made there.
3. **The metric counts users who make a `git`/`gh` commit.** A session that only edits files still won't register — that's inherent to how the signal is collected, not something this PR changes.

## How to validate manually

1. Enable the agent-host harnesses in Settings:
   ```jsonc
   "chat.agentHost.enabled": true,
   // makes the *agent-host* Copilot session type the one that surfaces,
   // instead of the extension-host one
   "chat.agents.copilotCli.hideExtensionHost": true,
   // only if you also want to check Codex
   "chat.agentHost.codexAgent.enabled": true
   ```
   Restart VS Code (the agent host process must be restarted to pick these up).

2. Create a scratch folder with this script in it:
   ```sh
   # probe.sh
   #!/bin/sh
   echo "AI_AGENT=$AI_AGENT"
   ```

3. Open the Agents window, start a **new** session in that folder, and pick the session type from the `with …` picker (**Copilot**, **Codex**, or **Claude**).

4. Send: `Run this shell command: sh ./probe.sh` and approve the confirmation.

5. Expected output: `AI_AGENT=github_copilot_vscode_agent` for Copilot and Codex. For Claude, expect `claude-code_<version>_agent` (see caveat 1).

Notes for verification:
- Be sure to use a **new** session created after the restart — a resumed session may be served by the older harness.
- If the composer placeholder still says "Run tasks in the background with the Copilot CLI", you're on the extension-host harness; double-check `chat.agents.copilotCli.hideExtensionHost` and restart.
- Cross-check without a chat at all: find the agent host process and its CLI child and dump their environments, e.g. on macOS/Linux `ps eww -p <pid> | tr ' ' '\n' | grep AI_AGENT`.

title: sessions: support mouse back/forward buttons in the Agents window
body:
Fixes #327434

## Problem

The mouse back/forward buttons navigate editor history in the main VS Code window, but did nothing in the Agents window — even though the `Alt+Left` / `Alt+Right` keybindings already navigated between sessions there.

## Root cause

The shared mouse handler in `HistoryService.onMouseDownOrUp` calls `goBack()` / `goForward()` on the **editor** history service directly:

```ts
case 3:
    EventHelper.stop(event);
    if (isMouseDown) { this.goBack(); }   // service call, not a command dispatch
```

Because it bypasses command/keybinding resolution entirely, no `when`-clause routing applies. That is exactly why the keyboard path worked while the mouse path did not: the Agents window has its own session history (`SessionsNavigation`, exposed via `ISessionsService.openPreviousSession()` / `openNextSession()`), and the editor history the mouse fell through to is usually empty there.

Note this is not a case of "the Agents window forgot to reuse the editor commands". Both histories are deliberately live in that window — editor history still matters for the docked side pane (Changes multi-diff, Files, file diffs) — and the two are disambiguated by focus via `EditorAreaFocusContext`. The gap is only that mouse buttons don't go through the same dispatch as their keybindings.

## Changes

- **New `SessionsMouseNavigationContribution`** (`src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/browser/sessionsMouseNavigation.ts`): a capture-phase `mousedown` / `mouseup` listener on each workbench container that routes buttons 4/5 to session history when focus is **outside** the editor area. It stops propagation so the shared bubble listener does not also navigate editor history, and suppresses `mouseup` so the browser's own back/forward does not fire.
- **Editor focus is left untouched.** With the editor area focused the events pass through unchanged, so the docked side pane keeps its normal editor-history behavior.
- **Setting is honored.** `workbench.editor.mouseBackForwardToNavigate` still gates the behavior. Its key is now an exported `MOUSE_BACK_FORWARD_NAVIGATION_SETTING` constant in `services/history/common/history.ts`, shared by `HistoryService`, the configuration registration, and the new contribution instead of being duplicated as a string literal.
- **Keybindings:** added `BrowserBack` / `BrowserForward` as secondary bindings for `sessions.goBack` / `sessions.goForward`, matching `NavigateBackwardsAction` / `NavigateForwardAction`.
- **Accessibility:** documented Go Back / Go Forward in the Agents window accessibility help dialog (per the `accessibility` skill's rule that new commands must be discoverable there).
- **Docs:** noted the routing rule in `src/vs/sessions/SESSIONS.md`.

## Tests

New `sessionsMouseNavigation.test.ts` covers the three behaviors that matter:

1. Buttons 4/5 navigate session history once per press, and the event neither bubbles to the shared listener nor reaches browser history.
2. With the editor area focused, events pass through untouched and no session navigation occurs.
3. Toggling `workbench.editor.mouseBackForwardToNavigate` disables/enables handling.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client` — pass
- `npm run valid-layers-check` — pass
- hygiene on all changed files — pass
- `sessionsMouseNavigation.test.ts` — 4 passing
- `sessionNavigation.test.ts` — 18 passing (no regression)
- `historyService.test.ts` — 23 passing (no regression)

## Note for reviewers

A cleaner long-term fix would be to have the `HistoryService` mouse handler dispatch `workbench.action.navigateBack` / `navigateForward` through `ICommandService` so `when` clauses decide the target. Any window contributing higher-weight bindings for those chords would then get mouse support for free, and this sessions-specific listener could be deleted. That touches shared workbench behavior, so I kept this fix scoped — happy to switch approaches if preferred.

(Written by Copilot)

title: sessions: never select a harness the picker doesn't offer
body:
## Problem

While running the experiment that replaces the extension-host Copilot CLI with the Agent Host one:

```jsonc
"chat.agents.copilotCli.hideExtensionHost": true,
"chat.agentHost.enabled": true,
"chat.agentHost.defaultSessionsProvider": true,
```

switching to an extension-host session in the Agents window and then going back to the new chat page left the **extension-host agent selected**, even though it is hidden from the harness picker. You should never be able to have an agent selected that isn't actually offered in the picker.

## Root cause

Two "remember the previous agent" mechanisms compounded.

**1. The New Session gestures inherit the previous session's harness unconditionally.**

`NewChatInSessionsWindowAction` (the New button and <kbd>Cmd+N</kbd>) passed the active session's `providerId` + `sessionType` straight to `openNewSession`. With the setting on, `CopilotChatSessionsProvider.getSessionTypes()` returns `[]`, so `_resolveProviderForNewSession` throws `does not advertise session type 'copilotcli'` — and `openNewSession` swallows it with only a trace log.

A throwaway unit test against the real `SessionsManagementService` / `SessionsService` confirmed the outcome — nothing is created on *either* provider, the folder is dropped, and the composer lands session-less:

```
activeProviderBefore: 'copilot',  createdOnCopilot: [],  createdOnAgentHost: [],
draftProviderId: undefined,       activeAfter: undefined,
folderTypes: ['local-agent-host/copilotcli']
```

**2. With no session, the picker falls back to the stored pick without validating it.**

`SessionTypePicker._computeCurrentPick()` returned either the session's `{providerId, sessionTypeId}` verbatim or `_readStoredPick()` (`sessions.userSelectedSessionType`) — never checking either against `_folderSessionTypes`, the list the dropdown actually renders. So the remembered `{providerId: 'copilot', sessionTypeId: 'copilotcli'}` shows as selected while being absent from the picker.

## Changes

- **`sessionsManagement.ts`** — new shared `inheritableSessionTarget()` helper: carry the harness over only while `isNewSessionTargetAvailable()` says the folder still offers it, otherwise fall back to the folder's preferred harness.
- **`chat.contribution.ts` / `sessionsService.ts`** — both "carry the harness over" sites (New Session, and the archived-session fallback) now route through that helper. New Session keeps the folder and lets the Agent Host's Copilot serve it.
- **`sessionTypePicker.ts`** — new `_offeredPick()` constrains the displayed pick to the offered types. Applied to the stored pick and to *uncommitted drafts*.
- **`newChatWidget.ts`** — `_replaceDraftOnUnservableHarness()` recreates a restored draft whose harness the folder can no longer serve, so the composer can't show one agent while sending to another.

## Notes for reviewers

Two deliberate carve-outs, both covered by tests:

- A **committed** session keeps displaying the harness it genuinely runs on, even if that harness is no longer offered for *new* sessions — the picker should tell the truth about an existing session.
- An **empty** type list means the folder's providers haven't reported yet (a late-connecting agent host), so the pick/draft is left alone. This preserves the existing late-discovery behaviour that `_scheduleRecreateOnProviderChange` and the "preserves an unavailable initial pick until its provider appears" tests rely on.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client`, hygiene, and `npm run valid-layers-check` are clean.
- All **1659** `src/vs/sessions` unit tests pass, including 4 new regression tests:
  - `a draft never displays a harness the picker no longer offers`
  - `a committed session keeps displaying the harness it runs on`
  - `a stored pick for a hidden harness does not survive into an offering picker`
  - `inheritableSessionTarget drops a harness the folder no longer offers`

Not verified by running the app: `npm install` fails on `extensions/copilot`'s private registry here (`npm error code E401`), so the extension-host Copilot CLI side isn't buildable in this environment. Everything above is verified at the unit level against the real services. Worth a manual pass with the experiment settings before this leaves draft.

(Written by Copilot)

Fixes #327429

title: Harden Agent Host E2E and protocol integration tests
body:
Hardens the Agent Host E2E and protocol integration tests following the failures reported in [this PR comment](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/327213#issuecomment-5064384775).

## Changes

- use platform-aware protocol operation timeouts with extra Windows and coverage headroom
- register pending JSON-RPC calls before sending to avoid fast-response races
- centralize bounded graceful server shutdown with forced termination fallback
- await server shutdown across protocol suites to avoid process overlap
- track and clean up secondary WebSocket clients on failure paths
- replace wall-clock sleeps with protocol barriers and turn-specific notification matching
- add retry-backed temporary resource cleanup for Windows

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client`
- `npm run precommit`
- Agent Host protocol integration tests: 115 passing, 1 pending
- reported terminal E2E cases for Claude: 2 passing
- reported terminal E2E cases for Copilot: 2 passing
- final code review: no findings

(Written by Copilot)

title: Add Claude Opus 5 system prompt
body:
Adds a minimal system prompt for Claude Opus 5, gated behind `github.copilot.chat.claudeOpus5Prompt.enabled` (experiment-based, off by default). When off, Opus 5 falls back to the existing Claude 4.6 Opus prompt.

### The new prompt

Built following Anthropic's guidance for the Claude 5 generation — describe the environment as facts rather than as a list of rules, and put the behavioral weight into scope and correction guidance instead of prohibitions. It keeps six sections: `instructions`, `harness`, `deliveringWork`, `operationalSafety`, `communication`, and `outputFormatting`, plus the MCP, notebook, linkification, and translation pieces the UI depends on.

What's deliberately **not** in it: separate verification passes, over-engineering and comment policies, task-tracking rules, and worked examples. Anthropic's guidance is that this generation handles those with its own judgement, and that verification instructions in particular cause *over*-verification. Context compaction is assumed off for this model, so there's no `contextManagement` section.

### Also in this change

- **Removed the Opus 4.8 and Sonnet 5 prompts** and their settings (`claude48OpusPrompt.enabled`, `claudeSonnet5Prompt.enabled`). Both models now use the Claude 4.6 prompts.
- **Comment-etiquette guidance** added to `AnthropicReminderInstructionsOptimized` rather than to a single prompt, so it reaches every Claude 4.6+ family. This is what moves the 22 snapshots — the added line is the only delta in each.
- **Tool search enabled for `claude-opus-5`.**

title: sessions: Refine the prompt sticky header (styling, navigation, roll)
body:
Polishes the Agents-window prompt timeline **sticky header** (introduced in #326861). All changes are scoped to `src/vs/sessions/contrib/promptTimeline/` (plus a one-line accessibility-help update and a spec note).

### What changed

**Styling — align with the VS Code standard and the session header**
- Replace the hover **underline** on the sticky title with the standard **hover background**, using the chat request-bubble tokens (`--vscode-chat-requestBubbleHoverBackground`), with padding + a control-tier radius for breathing room.
- Give the band the chat request-bubble **background** (composited over the opaque panel base so it stays opaque over scrolling rows).
- Mirror the **session header's box model** so the band lines up with the header's bottom-border line above it: a centered 950 host with the header bar's 10px side padding (`.session-view-centered-content` + `.chat-composite-bar.session-header-bar`), and an inner band that carries the background/border/shadow (like `.chat-composite-bar-header`). A left inset of `codicon size + 6px gap` reproduces the header's status-icon column so the prompt text stays aligned with the title and the prompts below. This also removed a ~1px right-edge "bump" where the previous full-width band overhung the scrollbar gutter.
- Round the band's **bottom corners** (control tier) and add **left + right borders** with an open top, so it reads as anchored to the top of the transcript and closing off at the bottom.

**Navigation — make it consistent**
- Previous/Next now reveal the prompt **row itself** (aligned to the top), exactly like clicking the sticky title and like the dock rail — previously they aligned the following response and pinned the header, which showed only a sliver of the target prompt.
- Removed the navigation-pin machinery; the header now consistently follows scroll tracking and hides after a jump.

**Transition — a lightweight "roll"**
- When the pinned prompt changes while the header is visible, the label text rolls (slide + fade of the outgoing/incoming line) via the Web Animations API, inside a clip viewport. The opaque band stays fixed (a full Explorer-style push-off would overflow above the transcript and clip the band's shadow). Snaps on first appearance/jumps and honors `prefers-reduced-motion`.

### Notes for reviewers
- **Performance:** profiled a scroll-heavy DevTools trace — the roll and reveal animations are 100% GPU-composited (0 composite failures) and the sticky header contributes ~0 to style-recalc/layout (`prompt-timeline` appears in 0 of the 888 `UpdateLayoutTree` events). Total main-thread cost attributable to the band across ~7.3s is ~3ms of paint.
- **Accessibility:** the accessibility-help entry for the prompt timeline was updated to mention activating the pinned title / Previous & Next buttons. The band's `<button>` + toolbar actions keep their labels/roles; transient roll lines are governed by the button's `aria-label`.
- No new tests: this is UI polish on an existing feature. Manual verification suggested on a wide and a narrow window, with reduced motion on/off, and scrolling fast across many prompts.

title: agentHost: route steering messages to the chat they were sent in
body:
- Copilot's `setPendingMessages` resolved its target via `_findAnySession`, which always returns the session's default chat. A steering message submitted in a forked (peer) chat was therefore injected into the primary chat's SDK session, steering the wrong conversation and never reaching the intended one.
- Makes the chat URI the single, required addressing argument on `IAgent.setPendingMessages`. Previously the session URI was the primary argument with an optional `chat` override, which left an ambiguous session-addressed form that could silently land in an arbitrary chat. There is no case where pending messages should be set without naming a concrete chat channel.
- Claude and Codex are updated to the new signature so all harnesses share one addressing convention, and `AgentSideEffects` now forwards the chat channel it already has instead of downgrading the default chat to the session URI.

Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/326244

title: Avoid false positives in dictation cleanup validation
body:
Regression from #327224.

The dictation cleanup faithfulness guard split text only on whitespace and then removed punctuation within each token. Legitimate cleanup such as open source becoming open-source, em-dash formatting, apostrophes, or Unicode accent normalization could therefore look like a wording change and incorrectly fall back to the raw transcript.

This tokenizes Unicode word runs after normalizing accents and apostrophes. It continues to require cleaned words to appear in order and retain at least 60% of the transcript, preserving protection against generated HTML, generated prose, reordered text, and heavy truncation.

title: Fix hydrated image attachment previews
body:
Fixes #327299

## Summary

- reject URI-backed image attachments when coercing serialized inline bytes
- let the image carousel load hydrated attachments from their persisted file resource
- preserve support for contiguous numeric byte maps restored from older serialized sessions

## Why this is correct

Before send, pasted images carry inline `Uint8Array` data. Agent Host intentionally snapshots that data to disk, and history hydration restores the attachment as an image entry whose `value` is a `URI` and whose `references` point to the persisted file.

`coerceImageBuffer` is only responsible for recognizing inline bytes. Its previous object fallback accepted every object, so the seven enumerable fields of a `URI` became seven zero bytes. Because that result was truthy, Images Preview preferred the corrupt inline data and skipped its valid file-resource fallback.

The new validation accepts only the exact legacy serialized-`Uint8Array` shape: contiguous numeric keys starting at `0`, each containing an integer byte from `0` through `255`. Existing `Uint8Array` and `ArrayBuffer` paths are unchanged. URI and other structured objects now return `undefined`, which deliberately lets the existing resource path read the persisted image.

The regression test uses the hydrated shape (`value: URI` plus its resource reference), while the existing numeric-map tests ensure backward compatibility, including reordered numeric keys.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client`
- `npm run valid-layers-check`
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/common/chatImageExtraction.test.ts`
- focused hygiene checks
- reopened a hydrated Agent Host session and confirmed the sent image renders in Images Preview

title: Retry transient Agent Host database initialization
body:
This fixes a recovery issue exposed when an Agent Host machine temporarily runs out of disk space.

When the initial per-session SQLite open failed, `SessionDatabase` retained the rejected initialization promise. Long-lived session references would then continue returning the original `SQLITE_CANTOPEN` failure even after the filesystem became writable again.

The initialization promise is now cleared on any setup failure, allowing the next database operation to retry. A regression test covers an initially blocked database path becoming writable.

title: agentHost: stabilize resume fallback tests
body:
## Summary

Fixes #327214 and follows up on the flaky test disabled in #327213.

- restore immediate initial session customization discovery
- move Copilot resume-fallback coverage to the deterministic `CopilotSessionLauncher` boundary
- keep watcher-driven refreshes debounced

## Root cause

#325407 intentionally changed the initial discovery call to use a zero delay while keeping the 100 ms debounce for subsequent watcher refreshes. The long-running #325241 branch had started before that change and modified the same constructor. When it later merged `main`, the merge result retained the branch's older call without the zero-delay argument.

That made `_resumeSession` wait on debounced customization discovery. In the failing Windows CI run, this test first passed in 111 ms, then timed out at 2 seconds while the adjacent fallback test took 1.2 seconds, indicating runner load was stretching unrelated timer/filesystem work.

## Test changes

The three fallback tests previously called the full private `CopilotAgent._resumeSession` path. Although they only intended to verify the launcher's resume-error policy, they also exercised authentication, temp-directory creation, customization discovery and watchers, session database setup, agent-session construction, and async shutdown.

The fallback policy is implemented by `CopilotSessionLauncher.launch`, so the tests now invoke that boundary directly with a small fake SDK client:

- a realistic Start Over `-32603` / `no events` error must call `createSession` once
- an unknown `-32603` must call `createSession` once
- a corruption error must propagate and never call `createSession`

The assertions are unchanged in meaning, but the tests no longer depend on timers, filesystem discovery, SQLite, authentication, or agent teardown. Existing `CopilotAgent` tests continue to cover the agent-level resume path, including custom-agent restoration and retry behavior.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client`
- 139 tests across `copilotAgent.test.ts` and `copilotSessionLauncher.test.ts`
- fallback suite passed in 20/20 fresh Electron processes
- changed-file hygiene
- `npm run valid-layers-check`

title: Retire completed non-PTY shell output resources
body:
Resolves: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/327178
Follow-up to: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/327067

- Add idempotent retirement for completed non-PTY shell output resources, removing both the host resource and its tracked stream.
- Publish the final `ChatToolCallComplete` result before retiring the live output resource so completed rendering has an authoritative static result.
- Retire only when both an exit code and preview are available; an empty preview still counts as authoritative.
- Keep background and no-preview output streams session-owned until normal session disposal.
- Prevent completed static non-PTY results from attaching to an already-retired URI, while preserving normal turn-owned cleanup for attachments created during streaming.
- Add coverage for distinct shell-call URIs, empty previews, background output, session cleanup, completed history, and PTY compatibility.

-----------------------------------------
Inspirations from:

- Output-only terminal retirement uses the existing non-process cleanup path in [`AgentHostTerminalManager.disposeTerminal`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/b5240eab09c8fe52409431657b19e4cb3e2c8865/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentHostTerminalManager.ts#L884-L894).
- Completed terminal rendering already prefers structured `result.preview` through [`getTerminalOutput`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/b5240eab09c8fe52409431657b19e4cb3e2c8865/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/agentSessions/agentHost/stateToProgressAdapter.ts#L1163-L1184).
- Static terminal identity and output restoration follow [`buildTerminalToolSpecificData`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/b5240eab09c8fe52409431657b19e4cb3e2c8865/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/agentSessions/agentHost/stateToProgressAdapter.ts#L1280-L1326).

title: Reuse terminals when replacing new session drafts
body:
Resolves: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/327169

- Add `onDidReplaceNewDraftSession` for the workspace New Session → New Session lifecycle, distinct from draft graduation.
- Fire the event before publishing the replacement draft so terminal ownership moves before eager terminal creation.

title: Incrementally refine dictation transcripts
body:
Fixes #327222
Fixes #327219

## Summary

- periodically refine stable portions of the live dictation transcript instead of waiting until recording stops
- send at most 800 trailing characters per incremental request, with a five-second minimum interval
- preserve the previously refined display prefix while keeping the raw ASR transcript untouched for final cleanup and fallback
- cancel stale or overlapping refinement requests when dictation stops, is cancelled, or speech recognition revises the processed prefix
- reject cleanup output that adds or rewrites dictated words, preventing requests from being followed as instructions or turned into generated HTML/code
- ask post-processing to format dictated sequences as Markdown bullet or numbered lists

## How incremental cleanup works

While the user dictates, VS Code periodically sends a stable portion of the recent transcript to the cleanup model. During active transcription it leaves the newest 20 characters untouched because speech recognition may still revise them; after one second without an update, the complete live tail is considered stable, including short dictation. Cleaned text appears while recording continues. If speech recognition revises processed words, stale cleanup is cancelled and retried. When recording stops, the complete raw transcript receives the existing authoritative final cleanup pass.

Both incremental and final cleanup are controlled by `dictation.experimental.llmCleanup`. Disabling the setting turns off both behaviors.

The final cleanup retains its timeout, cancellation, length limit, output-faithfulness validation, and raw-transcript fallback behavior.

title: Voice: don't auto-send the turn by default when hands-free is disabled
body:
Fixes #327217

## What

When hands-free mode (`agents.voice.handsFree`) is **disabled**, voice mode no longer auto-sends the turn by default. Previously the turn ended automatically on trailing silence (`agents.voice.turn.silenceMs`, default `800`) and on a stop phrase (`agents.voice.turn.stopPhrases`, default `['send it']`) regardless of the hands-free setting, which is surprising for users who opt out of the automatic back-and-forth loop.

## How

In `voiceClientService._getTurnConfig()`:
- Read `agents.voice.handsFree`.
- When hands-free is disabled, suppress trailing-silence ending unless `agents.voice.turn.silenceMs` is **explicitly** configured, and suppress stop-phrase ending unless `agents.voice.turn.stopPhrases` is explicitly configured (via `IConfigurationService.inspect()`).
- Users who explicitly set either setting keep that behavior; the derived `auto_end_mode` becomes `off` only when nothing opts in.

Also:
- Re-send the turn config to the backend when `agents.voice.handsFree` changes (previously only silence/phrase changes triggered a resend).
- Update the setting descriptions for `agents.voice.turn.silenceMs`, `agents.voice.turn.stopPhrases`, and `agents.voice.handsFree` to document this.

## Notes

- No behavior change when hands-free is enabled (the default), or when the turn settings are explicitly configured.
- Draft.

title: Experimental: clean up dictation transcript with a language model
body:
Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/327205
Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/327204

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6d0d5525-9840-4104-910a-4d66d051a9db

## Clean up dictation transcript with a language model

Our built-in on-device dictation (streaming Nemotron ASR via Foundry Local) emits lowercase, largely unpunctuated text and transcribes filler words verbatim, so dictated input reads as one long run-on. The underlying model and the Foundry SDK expose no punctuation option, so this runs the final transcript through a small language model to restore formatting.

### How it works
- Setting **`dictation.experimental.llmCleanup`** (on by default, experimental).
- After the raw transcript is produced, `ChatSpeechToTextService.stopAndTranscribe()` sends it once to `copilot-utility-small` (via `ILanguageModelsService`) with a strict "only fix punctuation, casing, spacing, and paragraphs; preserve wording; drop fillers/false starts; never answer" prompt, then returns the cleaned text.
- Robust and non-blocking:
  - Owns a per-cleanup `CancellationTokenSource` with a 10s deadline; cancelled from `cancel()`. If the session is aborted mid-cleanup, `stopAndTranscribe()` bails without touching shared state, so it can never get stuck in `Transcribing` or tear down a newly started session.
  - Transcripts over the 4000-char cap skip cleanup and return raw (no truncation).
  - The response stream is consumed with strict error propagation and `await response.result`, so only a complete response can replace the transcript — a mid-stream failure falls back to the raw transcript.
  - `finalizeMs` telemetry is measured after cleanup so it reflects model latency.

### Gating
Programmatically gated on Copilot: with AI features disabled, `selectLanguageModels` returns none and cleanup is skipped, falling back to the raw transcript.

title: Improve built-in dictation by filtering filler words
body:
Fixes #327205

## Improve built-in dictation punctuation and remove filler words

Our on-device dictation (streaming Nemotron ASR via Foundry Local) emits lowercase, largely unpunctuated per-segment text, and transcribes speech disfluencies verbatim. The result reads as one long lowercase run-on sentence full of "um" and "uh".

Added `localTranscriptionService.test.ts` covering run-on splitting, short-pause joins, no double-punctuation, "i" → "I", null-timing fallback, filler stripping/variants, filler-only segments, and preservation of filler-like real words.

title: fix: guard undefined stdio command in MCP server identity (fixes #327148)
body:
### Summary `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'includes')` thrown from `McpServer._hasUnresolvedVariables` (`src/vs/workbench/contrib/mcp/common/mcpServer.ts:745`). The MCP policy-governance layer builds an `IMcpServerIdentity` from a stdio launch via `_identityFromLaunch` as `command: [launch.command, ...launch.args]`. Although `McpServerLaunch.Stdio.command` is typed `string`, discovery/config producers assign it directly from untrusted configuration (e.g. `pluginMcpDiscovery._toLaunch` and `nativeMcpDiscoveryAdapters` use `command: config.command` / `command: server.command`). When a user's stdio MCP entry omits `command`, that value is `undefined`, so the produced `identity.command` array contains an `undefined` element — violating `IMcpServerIdentity.command: readonly string[]`. The new policy check `_hasUnresolvedVariables` then calls `arg.includes(...)` on that `undefined` element and throws inside the reactive `_policyBlock` autorun during `McpService.updateCollectedServers`. Fixes microsoft/vscode#327148 Recommended reviewer: `@vijayupadya` ### Culprit Commit `e1b18379` — "Add enterprise allowedMcpServers / deniedMcpServers governance policies for MCP servers" (PR #326226) by `@vijayupadya`, milestone 1.130.0 (matches the reported regression version). This PR introduced the identity-based policy matching flow (`_identityFromLaunch`, `_hasUnresolvedVariables`, `_policyBlock`) that first calls `.includes()` over the identity command elements. Before this feature an `undefined` stdio command never reached a string method on this path. ### Code Flow ```mermaid flowchart TD A[MCP config/discovery omits 'command'] --> B[McpServerLaunch.Stdio.command = undefined
despite typed string] B --> C[_identityFromLaunch builds
command: [undefined, ...args]] C --> D[_policyBlock derived autorun] D --> E[_hasUnresolvedVariables] E --> F["identity.command.some(arg => arg.includes(...))"] F --> G[TypeError: reading 'includes' of undefined] ``` ### Affected Files - `src/vs/workbench/contrib/mcp/common/mcpServer.ts` — `_identityFromLaunch` produces the `IMcpServerIdentity` whose command array is consumed by the policy check. ### Repro Steps 1. Configure a stdio MCP server whose entry lacks a `command` field (or where the resolved command is `undefined`). 2. Let the workbench collect MCP servers (`McpService.updateCollectedServers`), constructing `McpServer` and evaluating `_policyBlock`. 3. `_hasUnresolvedVariables` iterates `identity.command`, hits the `undefined` element, and throws `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'includes')`. ### How the Fix Works **Chosen approach** (`src/vs/workbench/contrib/mcp/common/mcpServer.ts`, `_identityFromLaunch`): build the identity's command array excluding an absent command. This fixes the value at the point where the `IMcpServerIdentity.command: readonly string[]` contract is established (the sole producer of the identity object), rather than guarding the crash site inside `_hasUnresolvedVariables` or the policy-matching utilities. The data-producer principle applies: the invalid array must not be created in the first place, so every downstream consumer (the unresolved-variable check and `checkMcpServerAllowed`'s command `equals` match) receives a well-typed string array. An explicit `!== undefined` check preserves a valid-but-empty command string, and `args` are defaulted to `[]` and filtered to strings so no non-string entry can reach the policy check. The `logService`/telemetry path is untouched and no `try/catch` masks the error. **Alternatives considered**: - Guarding inside `_hasUnresolvedVariables` (`arg => arg?.includes(...)`) — rejected: patches the crash site/typed consumer and leaves the malformed identity flowing into command-equality matching. - Filtering in each discovery adapter (`pluginMcpDiscovery`, `nativeMcpDiscoveryAdapters`, `installedMcpServersDiscovery`) — rejected as broader and duplicative; `_identityFromLaunch` is the single chokepoint that converts every launch into the identity the policy layer consumes, so one guard there covers all producers. ### Recommended Owner `@vijayupadya` — author of the culprit PR #326226 and owner of the MCP allow/deny governance policy code (`allowedMcpServers`, `_identityFromLaunch`, `_hasUnresolvedVariables`). > Generated by [errors-fix](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-engineering/actions/runs/30022364234) · 1.3K AIC · ⌖ 34.7 AIC · ⊞ 71K · [◷](https://github.com/search?q=repo:microsoft%2Fvscode+%22gh-aw-workflow-id:+errors-fix%22&type=pullrequests) ### errors-fix-driver — cycle 2 **Trigger**: cron_check_failed · **Head**: `d6ea160f4d8ed36e4b8f11b20c0c3a5fc2ce0062` (`d6ea160`) | Item | Action | |------|--------| | Review on `mcpServer.ts:737` — sanitize non-string args (in scope) | Fixed in `d6ea160` (replied + resolved) | | Review on `mcpServer.ts:732` — comment names private method (in scope) | Fixed in `d6ea160` (replied + resolved) | | 3 prior review threads left unresolved by cycle 1 | Resolved this cycle (already addressed in `2367e68`) | | CI: `macOS / Electron` (failed on prior head `2367e68`) | New commit pushed; title: Add dictation backend selection; support for using MAI; rename dictation settings
body:
## Dictation backend selection + settings cleanup

Adds a cloud dictation backend option and regroups the dictation settings under a generic `dictation.*` namespace, since these settings govern dictation across chat, editor, and terminal — not just chat.

### Settings

| Old | New | Change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `chat.speechToText.model` | `dictation.model` | Renamed; adds a cloud **`mai`** option alongside the on-device Nemotron model. |
| `chat.speechToText.enabled` | `dictation.enabled` | Renamed to a generic dictation kill-switch. |
| `chat.speechToText.mode` | _(removed)_ | The shortcut now always uses the former `auto` behavior: tap toggles, hold is push-to-talk. |

Settings migrations map any stored `chat.speechToText.*` values (including legacy on-device model ids) to the new keys, preserving an already-configured destination value (e.g. after settings sync) and clearing the removed `mode` key.

### Backends

- **`nemotron-speech-streaming-en-0.6b`** (default): on-device, via `ILocalTranscriptionService` (Foundry Local). Offline; no audio leaves the device.
- **`mai`**: cloud, via `IVoiceClientService` — the same voice service Voice Mode uses. Streams PCM16 over the voice websocket (PTT), authenticated with the GitHub token. Requires network + sign-in.

Selecting `mai` routes dictation start/stop/audio through the voice client instead of the local transcription service; nemo remains the default.

**Shared-connection safety** (the voice socket is a single connection shared with Voice Mode):
- Refuses to start when the socket is already connected, and only disconnects a connection this dictation established — so dictation and Voice Mode can't tear down each other's session.
- Requires GitHub sign-in (fails with an actionable message) before connecting rather than opening an unauthenticated socket.
- Filters transcription events by `turnId` and drops non-increasing `revision`s, so a late/other-turn event can't corrupt the transcript or resolve the final waiter early.
- Subscribes to `onFatalDisconnect` (terminal close codes 4001/4008/4029, e.g. another window took over) and fails/tears down the session — closing the mic — with a user-facing message.

### Telemetry (backend comparison)

The goal is to A/B compare the two backends, so dictation emits two events sliced by `backend` (`nemo` / `mai`) and `surface` (chat / editor / terminal).

**`chatSpeechToText.session`** — usage, reliability, and latency:
- `timeToFirstTranscriptMs` — first streamed audio → first transcript; isolates backend transcription latency (excludes mic acquisition + model download).
- `finalizeMs` — stop → final transcript; the post-stop wait.
- `partialUpdates` — count of interim (non-final) updates; a churn/stability proxy.
- plus existing `outcome`, `segments`, `transcriptLength`, `errorCode`.

**`chatSpeechToText.accuracy`** — a ground-truth-free accuracy proxy: how much the user edits dictated text before sending it. After a dictation finalizes, the dictated span is followed with a tracked decoration; the diff is measured at the **actual submit** (a `notifyDictationSubmitted` hook in the chat input part and the Agents composer send path, before the editor clears), falling back to clear/teardown otherwise:
- `dictatedLength`, `editDistance` (Levenshtein), `editRate` (`editDistance/dictatedLength`, capped at 1; lower is more accurate), `edited`, and `submitted` (whether an actual send fired vs. a clear/teardown).

Only aggregate character metrics are logged — never any transcript text. Edits typed at the span's edges are excluded so unrelated appended text isn't counted.

Examples (`editRate` = `editDistance / dictatedLength`, capped at 1):

| Scenario | dictated → submitted | editDistance | editRate | edited |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Clean, sent as-is | `add a retry to the upload handler` → _(same)_ | 0 | 0.00 | false |
| One misheard word fixed | `fix the of by one error…` → `fix the off by one error…` | 1 | 0.03 | true |
| Mostly rewritten | `um open the setting is file` → `refactor the parser` | 22 | 0.82 | true |

Across many sessions, a better backend shows more `edited=false` and lower `editRate` on the rest; `submitted=true` rows are the trustworthy signal.

### Notes

- Whether the MAI backend requires an explicit `sendStartSession` before PTT transcription still needs verification against a live backend; draft until validated end-to-end.

title: Fix race condition in modal editor part singleton creation
body:
## Summary

Fixes a race condition in modal editor part singleton creation identified while reviewing #326885.

EditorParts.createModalEditorPart awaited the ModalEditorPart creation (wait this.instantiationService.createInstance(ModalEditorPart, this).create(...)) *before* assigning 	his.modalEditorPart. If createModalEditorPart was called concurrently (e.g. two callers racing to open a modal editor), both calls could pass the "reuse existing instance" check and each create its own ModalEditorPart, resulting in duplicate modal editor parts/groups and duplicate onDidAddGroup events.

## Fix

- Track the in-flight creation as a promise (modalEditorPartCreatePromise).
- If a creation is already in flight when createModalEditorPart is called again, await that promise and apply the caller's options to the resulting singleton instance instead of starting a second creation.
- Preserves existing option-update behavior for both the "already created" and "creation in flight" cases.

This does **not** include the separate stable-ID change from #326885 — that should land separately.

## Testing

- createModalEditorPart is race-proof: concurrent creation returns same singleton instance (new test in modalEditorGroup.test.ts) fires 3 concurrent createModalEditorPart() calls via Promise.all and asserts:
  - all three calls resolve to the exact same instance/group
  - only one onDidAddGroup event fires
- Ran the full Modal Editor Group suite (42 tests) - all passing.
-

title: Agents: let agents manage automations
body:
## Summary

Adds an Agents-window **Automations** client-tool set so agents can list, create, update, and delete scheduled automations without bypassing the user’s existing tool approval policy.

- `listAutomations` returns stable IDs, editable fields, targets, and timing metadata.
- `configureAutomation` creates or partially updates an automation. It **never opens the automation Create/Edit dialog**: calls requiring interaction use normal tool confirmation, while centrally auto-approved calls proceed directly. Both paths run the same validation and guarded mutation.
- `deleteAutomation` follows normal approval policy. Interactive calls show **Delete**/**Cancel**; centrally auto-approved calls delete without a custom-button value.
- Successful create/update calls render a secondary chat button such as **Created an automation: Morning review** or **Edited an automation: Morning review**. Activating it opens Customizations → Automations and expands, reveals, and focuses the affected stable ID.
- All writes continue through `IAutomationService`; tools never write storage directly.

The PR also makes the existing shared automation snapshot safe under concurrent window mutations. It does **not** add or migrate a database schema.

## Suggested review order

| Order | Area | Primary files | Verify |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Tool behavior | `src/vs/sessions/contrib/automations/browser/automationTools.ts` | Strict input parsing, current-session targets, standard confirmation metadata, direct create/update, Delete/Cancel semantics |
| 2 | Conflict safety | common + Sessions `automationService.ts` | One canonical editable-state definition, preparation→approval conflict detection, final guarded update, runtime metadata tolerance |
| 3 | Result UI | `chatService.ts`, `chatToolInvocation.ts`, `chatAutomationConfiguredResultSubPart.ts`, `chatToolInvocationPart.ts` | Success-only structured data, deterministic pill, keyboard-accessible button |
| 4 | Navigation + restore | AI Customization editor/list files; `stateToProgressAdapter.ts` | Open Automations, focus stable ID, live and restored Agent Host result reconstruction |
| 5 | Agent Host approval bridge | `copilotAgentSession.ts`, `agentHostSessionHandler.ts` | Allow all stamps setting-driven approval on direct client-tool-ready calls; local tool confirmation is skipped |
| 6 | Removed complexity | automation dialog contract/implementation, `chatInputPart.ts`, tools service | No agent-proposal dialog branch; no generic `confirmationReason` plumbing; manual dialog remains intact |
| 7 | Persistence | automation storage services, storage IPC, browser IndexedDB storage | Authoritative single-key CAS, retry/rebase, no unrelated-key writes or schema migration |

The focused test files mirror these layers; `automationTools.test.ts` is the best behavior-level starting point.

## Approval behavior

| Operation | Interaction required by current policy | Centrally auto-approved |
|---|---|---|
| List | Executes immediately | Executes immediately |
| Create/update | Shows normal tool confirmation, then validates and persists | Validates and persists directly |
| Delete | Shows Delete/Cancel confirmation | Deletes directly |

`LanguageModelToolsService` remains the sole workbench approval authority after hooks, enterprise restrictions, session permission level, per-tool settings, Agent Host preapproval, and Autopilot risk assessment. Automation code does not re-read or reinterpret those settings.

For Copilot Agent Host sessions, SDK **Allow all** mode directly readies client tools instead of producing a provider permission request. The ready action now carries `autoApproveBySetting`, allowing the existing Agent Host→workbench bridge to pass `preApproved` and avoid a second local confirmation. A plain protocol `not-needed` reason is deliberately not treated as setting approval because default-ready client tools can use the same reason.

Denial happens before `invoke`; cancellation, disabled Automations, invalid IDs/targets, and conflicts return without writing. Explicit targets must resolve through the live workspace or quick-chat session-type catalogs. Omitted or `currentSession` targets use the invoking Agents session.

## Update safety

There are two intentionally separate conflict boundaries:

1. `prepareToolInvocation` records the automation’s canonical editable state in transient preparation data. After approval, `invoke` re-reads the automation and rejects editable changes made while confirmation was pending. This data is omitted from serialized chat invocations.
2. `updateAutomationIfUnchanged` compares the same canonical editable state inside the authoritative ledger mutation. The storage CAS/retry loop closes the final invoke→persist race.

Runtime-only `updatedAt`, `lastRunAt`, and `nextRunAt` changes do not conflict, so scheduler progress is preserved. Editable changes fail closed and require `listAutomations` to refresh.

## Chat result flow

- Native live calls propagate `IToolResult.toolSpecificData` into `ChatToolInvocation` after a successful mutation.
- Native serialized chat keeps the structured `automationConfigured` result.
- Agent Host live completion attaches the same data in `finalizeToolInvocation`.
- Agent Host history reconstructs it from the successful `configureAutomation` JSON result, matching the existing `sessionCreated` pattern.
- Errors and cancellation never produce `automationConfigured`, so they cannot render a false success button.

The button reuses the existing quiet secondary result treatment, uses `Codicon.watch`, exposes localized visible/title text, and is fully keyboard operable.

## Persistence and corruption boundaries

The subsystem already stores definitions and retained run history together under application-scope key `chat.automations.ledger`. This PR retains that versioned snapshot.

Every mutation now performs:

1. authoritative raw read;
2. parse + record-scoped mutation;
3. retained-run trimming;
4. compare-and-swap of the exact old ledger value to revision + 1;
5. re-read and reapply on contention.

Desktop linearizes the comparison in the main-process storage channel. Web uses one IndexedDB `readwrite` transaction against the existing application database/fallback. Both paths touch only the automation key.

Safety invariants:

- no table, object-store, IndexedDB-version, or ledger-schema migration;
- no direct tool storage writes;
- no stale full-snapshot overwrite across windows;
- no unrelated-key enumeration, replacement, or deletion;
- no future-schema downgrade;
- automation deletion removes retained runs atomically while already-dispatched sessions continue independently.

## Manual dialog behavior

Agent configure calls no longer use the dialog. Manual Create/Edit still does. The independently useful behavior that automation workspace choices do not update new-session recents remains.

The final safety review found one manual-dialog cold-start race: late discovery of a saved custom mode could overwrite a mode the user selected while waiting. The retry now fails closed when the current mode has changed.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client`
- `npm run transpile-client`
- `npm run valid-layers-check`
- `npm run precommit`
- `git diff --check`
- Focused Electron suites for automation tools/service/dialog/runner/scheduler, central approval resolution, Copilot Agent Host client-tool permission propagation, Agent Host state conversion/client tools, chat result routing/accessibility, Automations list navigation, storage IPC/IndexedDB, and tool-set registration
- Two independent Claude Opus 4.8 long-context/max-reasoning reviews: bug/safety and architecture/overengineering. The single valid finding (manual mode retry race) is addressed; no blocking architecture or data-loss findings remain.

## Out of scope

- Changing scheduler cadence or leadership behavior
- Stopping an already-dispatched session when its automation is deleted
- Migrating persistence to per-record keys or a new database schema

title: Stream built-in shell output over AHP terminal channel
body:
Related: https://github.com/microsoft/agent-host-protocol/pull/352
Resolves: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/324825
Part of: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/323399

Adopts the terminal completion model from microsoft/agent-host-protocol#352 and supersedes the cumulative-Text approach from #326291.

- Re-vendor the pending AHP contract: remove `terminalComplete`, move `exitCode`/`preview`/`truncated` onto the terminal block as `result`, and add `isPty` to terminal tool results and terminal state.
- Stream public Copilot SDK `tool.execution_partial_result` events into output-only AHP terminal channels for runtime-executed shell tools, while leaving client-hosted PTY terminals on their existing path.
- Treat partial output as cumulative runtime snapshots: append only the unseen suffix while the snapshot grows, then clear and replay it when truncation rewrites the snapshot.
- Create the output channel before publishing its terminal block, including commands with no partial events; seed final preview data, persist the exit result, and keep background channels open until `shell_completed` supplies the real exit code.
- Attach non-PTY channels to chat through a read-only output source without creating an `ITerminalInstance`, adding a root terminal entry, opening a bottom-panel terminal, or exposing terminal Focus/Show actions.
- Render plain-text output in the existing detached xterm, normalize LF to CRLF only in the Agent Host output adapter, and serialize append/reset writes so streaming output is neither duplicated nor stale.
- Preserve live auto-expansion and running/completed command decorations for output-only tools while leaving the existing PTY decoration path unchanged.
- Reconstruct history with a stable non-PTY terminal URI and structured result, while retaining a structural fallback for old persisted `terminalComplete` blocks.
- Re-apply the local `CompletionItem.label` extension from #326807 after protocol generation. The generated snapshot still needs a final `.ahp-version` sync after microsoft/agent-host-protocol#352 lands.

-----------------------------------------
Inspirations from:

- The `isPty` and `result: TerminalCommandResult` shapes come from the protocol change itself: [`ToolResultTerminalContent`/`TerminalCommandResult`](https://github.com/microsoft/agent-host-protocol/blob/4c2e10105f13b1de659d3f253f8ad05fc48036a8/types/channels-chat/state.ts#L1398-L1432) and [`TerminalState.isPty`](https://github.com/microsoft/agent-host-protocol/blob/4c2e10105f13b1de659d3f253f8ad05fc48036a8/types/channels-terminal/state.ts#L110-L116).
- The attach-once terminal-block policy extends the existing PTY completion deduplication in [`copilotAgentSession`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/9aab2f51076649ada9d3d8412558fd1484dd5f04/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotAgentSession.ts#L3293-L3304).
- Updating terminal state before dispatching data, so late subscribers can reconstruct output from the snapshot, follows [`AgentHostTerminalManager._handlePtyData`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/9aab2f51076649ada9d3d8412558fd1484dd5f04/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentHostTerminalManager.ts#L608-L638).
- The output-only channel URI follows the existing Agent Host shell namespace in [`copilotShellTools`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/9aab2f51076649ada9d3d8412558fd1484dd5f04/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotShellTools.ts#L172-L179).
- Output-only auto-expansion reuses the command lifecycle semantics already used by the AHP terminal path in [`ChatTerminalToolProgressPart._attachAhpCommandSource`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/9aab2f51076649ada9d3d8412558fd1484dd5f04/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/chatContentParts/toolInvocationParts/chatTerminalToolProgressPart.ts#L926-L987).

title: gate nonpty terminal actions
body:
Summary
Fixes the inline terminal preview offering "Focus/Show Terminal" and a "view stale terminal" action for non-pty (SDK built-in / streaming) shell runs, where there is no real interactive terminal to focus.

The bug
The chat terminal preview (ChatTerminalToolProgressPart) decides whether to show the Focus/Show-Terminal action purely from whether a terminal instance exists (_toolbarHasInstance = !!terminalInstance), and its "open the terminal" fallback calls terminalService.openResource(terminalCommandUri). Neither has any notion of whether that terminal is a real interactive pty or an output-only, non-pty channel.

That distinction started to matter with the shell-output-streaming work (https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/327067): to stream output, a non-pty SDK shell run now emits a Terminal content block (agenthost-terminal://shell/copilotNonPtyShells/{toolCallId}, isPty: false). The adapter sets terminalToolSessionId for any Terminal block with no isPty guard, so a non-pty run now gets a terminalToolSessionId → a revived ITerminalInstance → _toolbarHasInstance === true → the Focus/Show action and the stale openResource fallback render. But these terminals are output-only: there is nothing interactive to focus, and "opening" them just surfaces an empty/stale terminal.

The protocol already carries the needed signal — isPty on ToolResultTerminalContent / TerminalState — but it was only consumed on the host side (agentHostPty uses it to set convertEol). It never reached IChatTerminalToolInvocationData, and the widget never gated any UI on it.

Approach
Propagate the existing isPty signal end-to-end to the renderer, and gate the instance-dependent affordances on it — rather than inventing a new heuristic in the UI. Output-only non-pty terminals keep their preview (command, decoration, streamed output) but drop the actions that only make sense for a real interactive pty.

Changes and why
stateToProgressAdapter.ts (buildTerminalToolSpecificData) and agentHostSessionHandler.ts (_reviveTerminalIfNeeded) — read isPty off the Terminal content block and carry it onto the invocation data, in both producers, via a shared getTerminalContentIsPty helper.
Why: the terminal payload is built in two places — the main builder (create / streaming refresh / finalize / history replay) and the async terminal-revive path — so both must set the flag for it to stay consistent across every lifecycle stage. ?? existing preserves it across streaming refreshes.

chatService.ts (IChatTerminalToolInvocationData) — add the isPty field.
Why: the renderer had no channel to learn a terminal was non-pty; this is the missing carrier.

chatTerminalToolProgressPart.ts — add a single _isNonPtyTerminal (isPty === false) check and use it to hide the Focus/Show Terminal action and early-return focusTerminal() for non-pty terminals. The early-return covers every caller — the toolbar button, the "Focus Most Recent Terminal" command, and the collapsible "Show" link — including the stale openResource(terminalCommandUri) fallback.
Why: for output-only non-pty terminals there is no interactive session to focus; showing the action or opening a stale/empty terminal is misleading. The command decoration and streamed output are unaffected — only the interactive affordances are withheld.

stateToProgressAdapter.test.ts — assert isPty is threaded from the block (false / true / unset) and that it survives a streaming-output refresh (the revive → refresh race).

Notes / not in scope
Command decoration and output streaming for these runs are handled by https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/327067 (exit code now lives on the terminal block result; output streams via the non-pty channel). This PR only removes the incorrect interactive affordances.
The isPty semantics match the protocol flag added in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/327067: false = output-only non-pty channel; true/absent = pty-backed (custom-terminal or local) — those keep Focus/Show.
Known gap / follow-up
The isPty data-threading is unit-tested, but the widget gating behavior itself — Focus/Show hidden and focusTerminal() a no-op for non-pty cards — has no direct test. ChatTerminalToolProgressPart is never constructed in the test suite, and doing so needs substantial service/DOM mock setup, so it was left as a follow-up rather than done here. The gating is currently covered by the adapter tests plus reasoning; a widget-level test should be added to lock it in.

title: sessions: fix Agents window hang with per-group editor limit of 1
body:
Fixes #327066

## What

Enforce `showTabs: 'multiple'` and `limit: { enabled: false }` on the single-pane editor part (`SinglePaneMainEditorPart`) via the existing `enforcePartOptions` API.

## Why

The single-pane docked tab bar keeps several managed editors open at once — the pinned Changes multi-diff tab, the Files placeholder, and any real file tabs (`[Changes][Files][file…]`). Two user settings break this layout:

- `workbench.editor.showTabs` set to `single`/`none` collapses the docked tab strip.
- `workbench.editor.limit` (especially `perEditorGroup: true, value: 1`) makes `EditorsObserver` auto-evict the least-recently-used tab. Since the managed tabs are pinned (not sticky), they get evicted, the managed-tab reconciliation reopens them, and the observer evicts again — an infinite open/close loop that hangs the renderer (the reported bug).

## Notes for reviewers

- Scoped to the single-pane editor part only; the user's `workbench.editor.showTabs` / `workbench.editor.limit` settings are untouched everywhere else.
- `limit: { enabled: false }` is sufficient because `EditorsObserver.ensureOpenedEditorsLimit` returns early when the limit is disabled, so the other limit fields are never read.
- The `showTabs` enforcement was already present; this PR adds the `limit` enforcement to close the hang.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

title: chat: segmented voice/dictation toggle with hold-to-talk and listen-button styles
body:
## Segmented Voice / Dictation input toggle — two interaction styles

Option A:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c09956a3-133e-46a2-84b9-3c3429195b7e


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/964adb82-716f-4ee8-94be-e1ff813e5304

Option B:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dc28cb69-eb4d-4010-89bc-cdd4658153e6






Replaces the two independent mic buttons in the chat input with a **single segmented control** that unifies Dictation and live Voice Mode, and adds **two selectable Voice Mode interaction styles** to compare. Everything is gated behind experimental settings and defaults off.

### Why
Watching people use Voice Mode for the first time, a recurring problem was ending up in *both* dictation and voice at once, and confusion about which button connects vs. toggles listening vs. disconnects. This unifies the two into one discoverable control with clear animated state feedback, and mutual exclusion so you can only be in one mode at a time.

### Settings
- `chat.voiceInputMode.segmentedToggle` (boolean, default `false`) — show the single segmented control instead of the two separate mic buttons.
- `chat.voiceInputMode.interactionStyle` (`holdToTalk` | `listenButton`, default `holdToTalk`) — how Voice Mode drives listening.

### The two interaction styles
1. **`holdToTalk`** — the voice button is push-to-talk: **hold** it (or the `Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+Space` keybinding) to talk, release to send; a **quick tap** turns Voice Mode off.
2. **`listenButton`** — the voice button is a **power toggle** (connect / disconnect, and starts listening on connect); a **separate person-voice button** toggles listening on and off in manual mode.

### Highlights
- Dictation and Voice Mode live in one constant-size housing; icons slide/collapse between states.
- Voice Mode renders as an animated **Device EQ waveform** that transforms by state: idle undulating wave, **blue** mic-reactive listening, **purple** TTS-reactive speaking, and a short "silent" hover preview for disconnect — colors match the input-box glow.

segmented control that unifies Dictation and Voice Mode, gated behind the
new `chat.voiceInputMode.segmentedToggle` setting (default off).

- Dictation and Voice Mode live in one constant-size housing; icons slide
  and collapse between states, and mutual exclusion prevents both modes
  from being active at once.
- Voice Mode renders as an animated Device EQ waveform that transforms by
  state: idle undulating wave, blue mic-reactive listening, purple
  TTS-reactive speaking, and a short 'silent' hover preview for
  disconnect. Listening/speaking colors match the input-box glow.
- Voice Mode becomes a power toggle (connect/disconnect on the same
  button); the manual-mode listen toggle uses the person-voice icon and
  only appears when not hands-free (agents.voice.autoSendDelay).
- Remove the Voice Mode settings gear from the voice widget/header.
- Add dev-only simulate + prototype walkthrough commands to preview all
  states and transitions without a live connection.

Legacy standalone voice/dictation buttons remain as the fallback when the
setting is off.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>", 'chat: add hold-to-talk and listen-button voice interaction styles

Build on the segmented Dictation/Voice toggle with two selectable Voice
Mode interaction styles, chosen via the new `chat.voiceInputMode.interactionStyle`
setting (default `holdToTalk`):

- holdToTalk: the voice button is push-to-talk — hold it (or the
  Cmd+Shift+Space keybinding) to talk and release to send; a quick tap
  turns Voice Mode off.
- listenButton: the voice button is a power toggle (connect / disconnect,
  starting to listen on connect) and a separate person-voice button
  toggles listening on and off in manual mode.

Fix live Voice Mode cutting off after a word: pttDown/pttUp now take a
force flag so hold-to-talk records a clean turn and finishes on release
without entering the short-tap toggle mode or the auto-send silence timer.

Also add per-style prototype walkthrough commands that drive the pill
bars, colors, hover previews and the real input-box glow so the
interaction styles can be compared without a live connection.

title: Stream built-in shell output over AHP terminal channel
body:
Related: https://github.com/microsoft/agent-host-protocol/pull/352
Resolves: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/324825
Part of: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/323399

- Adopt the terminal completion model from microsoft/agent-host-protocol#352: move command `exitCode`/`preview`/`truncated` onto the terminal result and distinguish PTY-backed terminals from plain-text output channels with `isPty`.
- Stream public Copilot SDK `tool.execution_partial_result` events from runtime-executed shell tools into output-only AHP terminal channels, while keeping client-hosted PTY terminals on their existing path.
- Treat partial output as cumulative runtime snapshots: append only the unseen suffix while a snapshot grows, then clear and replay it when runtime truncation rewrites the snapshot.
- Create an output channel on the first partial result or when foreground shell completion supplies retained output or exit metadata. Leave background shell handoff and completions with neither output nor exit metadata out of the inline terminal path.
- Prefer structured SDK `shell_exit` metadata for the command result. When the external SDK bridge removes that block, use the runtime's trailing shell-completion marker as a scoped non-PTY fallback for the exit code and retained preview.
- Attach output-only channels to chat through a read-only output source without creating an `ITerminalInstance`, adding a root terminal entry, opening a panel terminal, or exposing terminal Focus/Show actions.
- Render the plain-text stream in the existing detached xterm, normalize line endings only in the Agent Host output adapter, and serialize snapshot writes so growing or rewritten output is not duplicated or stale.
- Preserve live auto-expansion and running/completed decorations for output-only tools. Existing Local harness and Agent Host PTY terminal behavior remain on the original path unless `isPty === false`.
- Scope output-channel URIs by Agent Host session and tool call, and reconstruct completed history from the terminal's structured result.
- Re-vendor the generated protocol snapshot after microsoft/agent-host-protocol#352 lands and use its final commit for `.ahp-version`.

-----------------------------------------
Inspirations from:

- The `isPty` and `result: TerminalCommandResult` shapes come from the protocol change itself: [`ToolResultTerminalContent`/`TerminalCommandResult`](https://github.com/microsoft/agent-host-protocol/blob/4c2e10105f13b1de659d3f253f8ad05fc48036a8/types/channels-chat/state.ts#L1398-L1432) and [`TerminalState.isPty`](https://github.com/microsoft/agent-host-protocol/blob/4c2e10105f13b1de659d3f253f8ad05fc48036a8/types/channels-terminal/state.ts#L110-L116).
- Publishing a terminal block once extends the existing PTY completion deduplication in [`copilotAgentSession`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/9aab2f51076649ada9d3d8412558fd1484dd5f04/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotAgentSession.ts#L3293-L3304).
- Updating terminal state before dispatching data, so late subscribers can reconstruct output from the snapshot, follows [`AgentHostTerminalManager._handlePtyData`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/9aab2f51076649ada9d3d8412558fd1484dd5f04/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentHostTerminalManager.ts#L608-L638).
- The output-only channel URI follows the existing Agent Host shell namespace in [`copilotShellTools`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/9aab2f51076649ada9d3d8412558fd1484dd5f04/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotShellTools.ts#L172-L179).
- Output-only auto-expansion reuses the command lifecycle semantics already used by the AHP terminal path in [`ChatTerminalToolProgressPart._attachAhpCommandSource`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/9aab2f51076649ada9d3d8412558fd1484dd5f04/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/chatContentParts/toolInvocationParts/chatTerminalToolProgressPart.ts#L926-L987).

title: Sessions: chat timeline variant
body:
This pull request introduces several enhancements to the chat session timeline UI, specifically addressing user feedback regarding the display of prompt entries and the functionality of the sticky header.

### Changes Made:
- **Prompt Dots**: The dock now renders one dot per user prompt, ensuring that the number of dots corresponds directly to the number of prompts. This is achieved through a new `_renderDots(count)` method that updates the handle dynamically based on the number of prompts.
  
- **Sticky Header Navigation**: Clicking the sticky header now navigates directly to the corresponding prompt instead of executing the "go to symbol" command. This is implemented by adding a `revealActivePrompt()` method in the model, which aligns the active prompt to the top of the transcript.

- **Breaking Change**: The configuration setting `sessions.promptTimeline.rail` has been changed to accept only string values (`off`, `ruler`, `dock`), removing the previous boolean option for cleaner implementation.

### Validation:
- All changes have been validated through type checks, ESLint, and layer checks, ensuring no regressions or errors in the codebase.

To test the new dock functionality, set:
```json
"sessions.promptTimeline.rail": "dock"
```
and enable the sticky header with:
```json
"sessions.promptTimeline.stickyHeader": true
```

Please review the changes and let me know if further adjustments are needed.

title: Stabilize Agent Host rename E2E snapshots
body:
## Summary

- use the existing behavior snapshot profile for local `/rename` scenarios
- keep the meaningful user turn, title change, response, and turn-completion contract
- exclude asynchronous provider startup traffic such as `session/serverToolsChanged` and incidental `session/chatUpdated` notifications

## Diagnosis

A temporary five-iteration cross-platform CI loop reproduced an intermittent Linux Codex failure. Codex sometimes completed session materialization after the rename snapshot round began, inserting `session/serverToolsChanged` before the local rename traffic. The notification is unrelated to the rename behavior and made the protocol-profile snapshot order-dependent.

The next Codex iteration could then fail the test runner console-cleanliness check because the first mismatch left an `.actual` snapshot. Removing the initial mismatch removes that cascade.

After the fix, all five full provider iterations passed on Linux, macOS, and Windows. The temporary workflow loops have been removed from this PR.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client`
- `node build/next/index.ts transpile`
- regenerated affected snapshots via `AGENT_HOST_UPDATE_AHP_SNAPSHOTS=1`
- affected rename scenarios looped five times for Copilot, Claude, and Codex locally
- full provider suites looped five times on Linux, macOS, and Windows PR CI
- `npm run valid-layers-check`
- `npm run precommit`

(Written by Copilot)

title: sessions: open single-file diff directly from single-pane Changes view
body:
Fixes #327012.

## What changed

`SinglePaneChangesViewPane` forced every file click in the Changes view to open the aggregate multi-file diff editor, ignoring the shared single/multi-file decision logic and the Alt invert. This removes that hardcoded override so single-pane falls through to the same logic as the standard layout: it honors the `sessions.changes.openSingleFileDiff` setting (default off, so default behavior is unchanged) with Alt inverting the choice, reusing the existing `_openSingleFileDiffEditor()`/`_openMultiFileDiffEditor()` paths and change-resource abstractions.

Also, when a single-file diff is opened from Changes, it now shows the whole file by default instead of folding unchanged regions — that diff is opened to review one specific file, so nothing should be hidden by default (the aggregate Changes editor keeps its existing Expand/Collapse All actions for the multi-file case).

## Why

Previously, users in the single-pane Agents Window layout always had to open the aggregate Changes editor to see any file's diff — clicking an individual file never opened just that file's diff, unlike the existing editor-window experience.

## Testing

- `npm run typecheck-client` — 0 errors
- ESLint — clean
- Hygiene (pre-commit) — passed
- `src/vs/sessions/contrib/changes/test/browser` suite — all passing

title: Fix Voice Mode panel dictation misrouting to background chat editor
body:
Fixes #327024

## Problem

In Voice Mode with the **panel** chat input, running a request could send it to a **background chat editor** that had been focused earlier instead of the panel, with narration/updates following that background session.

## Root cause

`_chat.voice.acceptInput` routed to `IChatWidgetService.lastFocusedWidget`, which is only updated on a chat widget's `onDidFocus` and is never cleared on blur (only on dispose). After a chat editor was opened/focused it stayed the `lastFocusedWidget`, and because dictating in the panel voice input does not DOM-focus the panel's chat input, the request was dispatched to that stale editor — even though `_chat.voice.getCurrentSession` (reading the panel view pane's own widget) reported the panel.

## Fix

Only trust `lastFocusedWidget` while it still holds input focus (an intentionally focused chat editor); otherwise fall back to the panel view pane's own widget (`this._widget`), keeping the send target consistent with `_chat.voice.getCurrentSession`.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client` — clean
- eslint on changed file — clean
